terminology.visibility: action/service surface classification: 'advertised' = declared in a shipped SCPD document AND (at service level) present in the served device_description.xml serviceList (16 of 17 services, everything except AudioIn); 'hidden' = service omitted from the serviceList even though its SCPD ships (AudioIn only); 'internal' = callable on the wire but not SCPD-declared; supported class, EMPTY on this build (verified: all 205 canonical actions appear in their service's SCPD actionList)
terminology.reachability: 'callable' = dispatched to a real implementation; 'hidden-callable' = reachable by action name on the control path but not SCPD-declared: EMPTY on this build
terminology.fault_vocabulary_caveat: identical fault-code vocabularies across builds do NOT prove identical error behavior; a fault-code vocabulary delta claim is made only where control flow was also compared

canonical_action_records.definition: every action object under services.*.actions in this dataset; 195 unique action names (some names recur across services)

scpd_defined.definition: actions declared in shipped SCPD documents (opt/htdocs/xml/<Svc>1.xml actionLists): all 205 canonical records + 2 removed SystemProperties actions (ProvisionCredentialedTrialAccountX, ResetThirdPartyCredentials) that remain SCPD-advertised but have no canonical record because they are absent from the 86.x dispatch surface
scpd_defined.source: documentation.json visibility field + SystemProperties dispatch note

device_advertised.definition: SCPD-defined actions on the 16 service registrations present in the served device_description.xml serviceList; excludes AudioIn whose service is hidden (SCPD ships but service unlisted); includes the 2 stale SystemProperties advertisements

binary_dispatched.definition: canonical records that resolve to a binary dispatch path; 199 reach a real implementation handler (141 ptr-table 'direct', 57 id-table 'virtual', 1 strcmp chain) and 6 resolve to the AudioIn reject-all stub
binary_dispatched.source: documentation.json dispatch records; extractor action_tables carry 195 rows across 14 tables - the shared ConnectionManager table 0x10f118d4 binds both CM services (6 records from 3 rows) and QPlay dispatches via a strcmp chain rather than a table

implemented_actions.definition: binary-dispatched records whose dispatch reaches a real implementation (excludes the 6 reject-all stubs)

removed_stale.definition: SCPD-defined actions removed from the live dispatch surface in 86.x: 6 canonical records dispatched to the AudioIn reject-all 401 stub + 2 SystemProperties actions absent from the dispatch table entirely (a stub name lookup miss faults 401 identically, so wire behavior matches the stubs)

meta.scpd_crossvalidation: SCPD ground-truth cross-validation (post-rootfs-sweep): all 16 advertised services in opt/htdocs/xml/*.xml compared against the extracted dispatch/SV tables. ACTION PARITY 206/208: the only SCPD-only entries are the two known advertised-but-removed SystemProperties ops ProvisionCredentialedTrialAccountX + ResetThirdPartyCredentials; the 6 AudioIn actions advertise AND dispatch to reject-all 401 stubs, consistent with prior findings. STATE-VARIABLE PARITY: all SCPD names present in the binary tables; binary additionally dispatches UNADVERTISED SVs: Queue {QueueID,QueueOwnerID}, RenderingControl {HeightChannelLevel,RoomCalibrationBondedZoneInfo,SonarCalibrationAvailable,SonarEnabled}, hidden state variables served by handlers but never declared in SCPD. ARGUMENT PARITY: full arg-name match on spot-checked services (AVTransport all 42 actions). This validates the binary-driven extraction pipeline against the shipped advertisement files end-to-end.

There is no per-record enabled byte in this router: the prior enabled values were extractor artifacts that captured the next record's obj getter store. todo: Unresolved: the request ctor itself - the object at httpd_ctx+0x288 is written upstream of f_10352848 (httpd SOAP-envelope layer); 69 stw +0x288 sites exist image-wide across unrelated classes, so the producing store needs identification by object type, not offset. The +0xc8-dispatch vptr that would name the request class is still unlocated; slot semantics remain callsite-proven only.
request_vtable.provenance: Request object lifetime: the request object arrives as r5-in at main router f_101953c8 (zp-aa vfunc; table 0x10e97d5c), is forwarded as r5-in to fallback router f_1068bc0c (call at 0x101956e4), forwarded again as r5-in to the per-service name-dispatcher (e.g. ZGT vtable 0x10f113b0 slot +0x8 = f_10732ff8, which strcmp-scans the name table at 0x10f113dc), and finally forwarded as r4-in to the matched action impl (e.g. GetZoneGroupAttributes f_10733878 at slot +0x24). Per-service dispatch vtables carry one slot per action (ZGT: 11 slots). The request object is allocated by the UPnP HTTP request layer above the zp vfunc entry; its ctor does not form a direct addis/addi reference in .text.
resolved_findings: Resolved at boundary: no .text ctor stores either candidate vtable (0x10ebc650/0x10ebd234) - the request object is allocated by an out-of-line UPnP-stack component and only consumed here. Slot semantics stand from caller patterns: parse 0x08, commit 0x0c, fault 0x14, in-arg 0x1c/0x20, out-arg 0x24, ctx 0x34, finalize 0x38.

Established: the complete request-object call chain is proven from zp-aa vfunc entry through the fallback router and per-service name-dispatchers down to the action impl (see provenance). Per-service dispatch vtables are mapped (e.g. ZGT 0x10f113b0, 11 action slots, name table 0x10f113dc).

request-object provenance pushed one level deeper: the service-route loop f_10352848 calls entry->vfunc[0xc8](entry, f_1053cc50(in_ctx)) at 0x10352940-0x10352960; f_1053cc50 is a getter returning *(in_ctx+0x288) - so the UPnP request object lives in the +0x288 slot of the HTTP-side request context handed to the dispatcher. Additionally the vtable at 0x10f10e88 was proven to be the class-A arg-record vtable (slot +8 = setName f_1055eaf0 stw +0x50, +0xc = getName f_1055eb00, +0x44 = the name-table arg accessor f_1073181c calling both record allocators) - it is the arg container class, not the request class.
request_vtable.callsite_proof: Slot semantics confirmed at concrete callsites in GetZoneGroupAttributes f_10733878: req->vtable[0x34] at 0x107338b0 returns the ctx object (result->+0x6c non-null check, ->+0x178 = zone-group impl); req->vtable[0x08] at 0x107338e4 is the arg-parse call made before the action body; req->vtable[0x14] at 0x10733904 is raise-fault; req->vtable[0x24] at 0x107339ac is get/create out-arg record by name (r4 = literal "CurrentZoneGroupName", repeated for "CurrentZoneGroupID"); the returned out-arg record has its own vtable (slots +0x10/+0x24 called at 0x10733950/0x107339c0 - a different class).
request_vtable.dispatch_chain: zp->vfunc[0xc8] = f_101953c8 (the per-service route matcher over the "/XxxService/Control" table) is invoked by f_10352848, which iterates a service container (*(r30+4) entries, element accessor f_1053cc50) and calls each entry's route-handler vfunc until one claims the request. f_10352848 is called by dp_impl internal-dispatch functions f_103548f4 and f_10355628 (joinZone/ValidateBondedState forwarding paths). The HTTP request path reaches the same zp vfunc from the UPnP HTTP action layer.
request_vtable.disproven: CORRECTION: the previously-listed candidate vtables 0x10ebc650 and 0x10ebd234 are NOT the request vtable. Their slot+0x34 impl f_1035a760 reads this+0x1ac0 and returns an enum code (0x41a/0), not a ctx object; slots +0x0c/+0x14/+0x1c/+0x24 are lock-guarded field getters (mutex at this+0x268 via f_10988558/f_10988984) copying +0x1aa1(byte)/+0x1aa2(strlcpy string)/+0x1abc(halfword)/+0x1abe(byte). They are sibling vtables of a state/session class in the UPnP-stack family, not the request interface.

RemoveTrackFromQueue.description: Removes a single track from the queue. Impl f_102aa770: after the 718-gate it fetches the queue's current update-id via f_10149b24(session+0x2d890). A nonzero UpdateID argument must equal that current id or the action returns 0x404 (decimal 1028): optimistic concurrency; UpdateID=0 skips the check. Mode impl+0x4654 must be 1 or 2 (else 800). Seek.description: Repositions playback within the current transport source, dispatched to the zone-player engine as impl vfunc +0x34 -> f_102b95a8(engine,InstanceID,Unit,Target): queue/track ordinal seek (TRACK_NR) or time seek (REL_TIME absolute / TIME_DELTA relative).

stw r27,0x6ed8(r29) stores the (zero) InstanceID into the engine on success

Unit.description: Seek-mode token; the engine compares it with strcmp against a fixed set and interprets Target accordingly.
Unit.format: utf-8 text, buffer cap 1024 bytes (1023 chars + NUL)

special_values.TRACK_NR: target is a queue/track ordinal; only reached when engine mode field (this+0x4654) == 2 and capability bit 0x400000 is set, else 701
special_values.REL_TIME: target is an absolute time position (H:M:S); in stream mode always allowed, in indexed mode requires capability bit 0x200000; negative target rejected with 711 in indexed mode
special_values.TIME_DELTA: target is a relative time delta (H:M:S); same gating as REL_TIME; a zero delta is a no-op success in indexed mode

Unit.validation: strcmp chain in f_102b9088: indexed mode (engine+0x4654==2) accepts TRACK_NR/REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA (unknown -> 710 at 0x102b9320-0x102b9338); stream mode accepts only REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA (anything else -> 701 at 0x102b90e0-0x102b91b0). Missing or oversized argument faults 402 at the request layer.

evidence.notes: f_102b9088 stream path: strcmp Unit vs TIME_DELTA (0x10eb04c4) then REL_TIME (0x10eb04b8)
f_102b9088 indexed path: strcmp Unit vs TRACK_NR (0x10eb0498)

Target.description: Destination operand whose syntax depends on Unit: a decimal track ordinal for TRACK_NR, or a [-]H:M:S time for REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA.
Target.format: utf-8 text, buffer cap 1024 bytes (1023 chars + NUL)
Target.accepted_values: TRACK_NR: textual decimal whose strtol result lies in 1..65534. REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA: three u8-wrapping decimal components; computed value = h*3600+m*60+s seconds.

special_values.TRACK_NR text beyond 1..65534 (incl. Seek.events_triggered: No UPnP event is emitted synchronously by this path; the SOAP response is committed immediately after the engine accepts the request while the actual position/track change is applied asynchronously by the chsrc transaction or streamer session. Any LastChange/state-variable update therefore originates downstream of the async apply and is not statically proven in this path.
Seek.state_transitions: None synchronously. The accepted seek is queued/applied by the player engine after the call returns; decoder, position and track-index state change happen inside the async transaction/streamer path, not in this handler.
Seek.return_behavior: The impl returns an integer status. On 0 the wrapper commits an empty 200 OK via req vfunc +0x0c (0x102f9494). On nonzero the code is forwarded to the request fault path req vfunc +0x14 at 0x102f944c and surfaces as the UPnPError errorCode. Caveats: (1) the wrapper tests cr0 rather than r3 at 0x102f9440; impl epilogues' stack-canary xor. leaves cr0.eq=1 on normal return, so rc reaches the completion vfunc +0x0c with r4=rc which handles the status-bearing response - the +0x14 branch is effectively a fallback. (2) In stream mode rc==0 only proves a session object accepted the call; the session vfunc's byte result is captured to a flag that gates a log line (0x102b91d8) and is not reflected in the SOAP status - a rejected streamer seek still reports success. (3) In indexed mode rc==0 only proves the rchsrcreq was enqueued, not that the seek applied; a zero-magnitude time target returns 0 without enqueueing at all.

SetCrossfadeMode.description: Sets crossfade on/off. Impl f_102b99fc gate (718) then body f_102b9a0c: lock impl+0x458, log 'upnp'/'change crossfade', call f_102b26dc. The worker REQUIRES mode impl+0x4654==2 (indexed) - anything else -> 712 immediately. In indexed mode it further requires f_101471f0(impl+0x5dc)!=0 AND strncmp(current URI,'x-sonosapi-hls:',15)!=0 AND f_101475dc!=0 (crossfade-capable, non-HLS source). When the source cannot crossfade: arg==0 still succeeds silently, arg!=0 -> 712. When capable: a request record (f_1032e270 + f_1032e550(rec,arg,1)) is submitted via f_10255f64(impl+0x580); success clears impl+0x6ed8.

SetNextAVTransportURI.description: Sets the gapless next-track URI. Impl f_102af288: 718-gate, lock impl+0x458, then a hard mode gate: impl+0x4654 must equal 2 (indexed/queued mode); any other mode returns 800, so next-URI only works on queue playback. In mode 2 it calls worker f_102af1c8(engine, NextURI, NextURIMetaData), which stores the URI into the next-track record at impl+0x6edc/0x6ee0 (f_106faeb8), manages pending flags impl+0x754c/+0x75cd (cleared) and impl+0x764e (set), fetches the current source URI via f_10293270(impl+0x5dc) and compares it against the engine source name impl+0x3dc: when they differ, the URI is forwarded through the member/topology path (member obj impl+0x448 -> f_10765a00/f_10762c30/f_106fbef4, with "lookup of %s URIs for %s failed" topology logging on failure), i.e. the next-track request can be delegated to the actual playback member.

AddURI.description: Enqueues one track into an explicit queue. Wrapper parses QueueID (int), UpdateID (int), EnqueuedURI (string, cap 0x401), EnqueuedURIMetaData (cap 0x1001), DesiredFirstTrackNumberEnqueued (int), EnqueueAsNext (bool byte), then calls impl->v[+0x8](impl, QueueID, UpdateID, &URI, &MD, DesiredFirst, EnqueueAsNext, &out1,&out2,&out3,&out4) on the queue-manager: rc==0 emits the four outputs, nonzero goes to req->v[+0x14] as a SOAP fault. This is the Queue-service twin of AVTransport.AddURIToQueue but keyed by explicit QueueID.

QPlayAuth.description: QPlay authentication handshake (Tencent seed->code exchange, fully decoded): dispatcher f_1073a4f0 strcmp-matches 'QPlayAuth' -> exec f_1073a5d0. Exec calls req->v[+0x1c] to fetch arg 'Seed' (0x10f11d64), parses it via f_1056157c into a stack buffer capped at 0x80 bytes, then gates on req->v[+0x08] (parse-ok check) -> emits 402 (0x192) Invalid Args on failure; 401 (0x191) for unknown action names. On success it calls impl->v[+0x08](impl, seedBuf, codeOut, 0x80, midOut, 0x15, didOut, 0x15) where impl = req->member[+0x04]: Code buffer cap 0x80, MID and DID buffers cap 0x15 (20-char strings + NUL). Each output is emitted as an individual out-arg via req->v[+0x24] with names 'Code'(0x10eb95c4)/'MID'(0x10f11d6c)/'DID'(0x10f11d70), value serialized through the out-arg object's v[+0x10] emitter; response committed via req->v[+0x0c]. The Seed->Code transform lives inside the impl member fn (no literals, crypto inlined or via shared hash lib) and is the only undecoded part. NOTE: an earlier attribution of the compute fn to f_104666b4 was wrong - that fn is a MuseDebugInfo formatter ('%s, %u, %u, %u' @0x10f94c88, 'MuseDebugInfo' @0x10f94c98).

0x3a8.description: Implementation-capability field read at 24 load site(s); gates action behavior paths
0x3a8.effect: On rc_impl, +0x3a8 holds this zone member own DSP channel-position byte (assigned from bonded-config byte 0). It is a data value propagated into dspStateManager::setParam as the per-channel record index, not a capability predicate. The name-keyed channel slots +0x7f1..+0x7f4 {Master,LF,RF,FocusMode} hold per-channel byte values for the WithoutProxy volume/mute setters.
resolved_findings: Established: +0x3a8 resolves per class - on the audio-settings object it is a u8 selector byte propagated into DSP state setters (leaf f_10d8d93c writes the halfword arg into a 0x20c-stride record); the stw catalogue entries are vptr slots on unrelated classes at the shared offset. Still unknown: the byte's exact enumeration (which DSP source/channel each value selects) - the setter leaf shifts it into a record index. Next step: enumerate values written by the stb stores to name the selector vocabulary.

Producer chain completed as far as static evidence reaches: the ctor f_100df3fc loads the incoming record pointer from stack+0xf8 (lwz at 0x100df47c), reads byte 0 of that record (lbz r26,0(r3) at 0x100df494), and stores it to +0x3a8 (stb at 0x100dfa30). The record is the member bonded-configuration blob delivered at rc_impl construction; byte 0 is the member channel-position assignment. On model-9/Playbar the bonded-role query f_101b4e50 is a compiled-out return-0 stub (satellite/stereo-pair roles exist only in the model-8 fenway vocabulary: UNBONDED_DEVICE, BONDED_STEREOPAIR, BONDED_TO_SUB, BONDED_STEREOPAIR_AND_SUB, HT_BONDED_SATELLITE), so the concrete byte-0 values assigned by the bonded-config negotiator are not present in this image. Boundary: the index-to-physical-position mapping (master/LF/RF/sub/surround) is produced by the bonded-zone negotiation protocol, absent on this model.
0x3a8.owning_class: rc_impl (RenderingControl impl object, ctor f_100df3fc in rc_impl.cxx) - the +0x3a8 field is this zone member DSP channel-position byte

value.consumer: read by the f_102a5xxx setter thunks and forwarded through f_107f5e38 into f_10d8d93c = dspStateManager::setParam(selector,value): the byte multiplies by 0x20c to index a per-channel DSP record array in the dsp manager (this+0x34+0xe0), writes the halfword at record+0x2ec, then f_10d8d8a8 walks the observer list (+0x8c..+0xe4) calling vptr+0x30
value.vocabulary: the byte is a runtime DSP-channel index, not a literal enum: channel-name->slot helpers f_100d99b0/f_100d9d40 key {Master,LF,RF,FocusMode} to per-channel value bytes at +0x7f1..+0x7f4 (written by SetMuteWithoutProxy 0x100db3fc and SetVolumeAndMuteWithoutProxy 0x100db5bc, read by channelName lookup f_100d71e0); index values are assigned from the bonded layout ('BONDED_STEREOPAIR_AND_SUB' family literals) so the concrete enumeration is config-dependent

Every other site is a different class member: two container begin pointers, a lazy-init ptr, DIDL flag bytes, bonded-layout u32, chproc audio-state field, a 0x21-char name buffer, curl members, topology_base member, zp field, and stack-canary frame slots.

0x5704.description: Implementation-capability field read at 24 load site(s); gates action behavior paths
0x5704.effect: zp+0x5704 is the low byte of the device-model feature-flags word (+0xd0) on the product descriptor singleton, taken at zp-aa construction from the singleton getter and propagated into per-request SOAP context. It is a device-model capability byte, not a per-request computed predicate.
resolved_findings: Established: zp+0x5704 is a ctor-arg-derived config byte propagated into the SOAP per-request record. Still unknown: which config dimension it encodes (the +0x56fc..+0x5702 cluster suggests device/capability id fields). Next step: trace the ctor-arg source word (callers of f_1018d27c, arg slot 0xc4) to name the flag.

Named: zp+0x5704 is the device's audio-input-present capability. The producer chain: product-descriptor singleton 0x110b8150 flag word +0xd0 -> low byte +0xd3 -> booleanized by f_10908540 (returns byte!=0) -> caller f_100c1478 supplies it as the first stack arg -> zp-aa ctor f_1018d27c stores it at zp+0x5704 (0x1018dc70) -> SOAP router copies it into each request record at 0x101955b0.

Feature gated: in the UPnP service-registration builder (0x10433xxx), the same f_10908540 result at 0x10433318 selects the registration branch that emits '/AudioIn/Control' + 'urn:schemas-upnp-org:service:AudioIn:1' (target 0x10433a70). Nonzero byte -> AudioIn service exists; zero -> it is never registered. This matches the record's affected_services=[AudioIn].

Flag-word structure: +0xd0/+0xd4/+0xd8 are a 3-word capability bitfield on the MDP-populated product descriptor (product names {S43,ZP120,ZP90,BR200,S1,Sub,S3}, model codes A100/A200/A101/A102/B100/D100/C201/C100/X999/C200). Enumerated accessors: +0xd0 bit16 (andis.0x1 gate in f_109085a8 -> +0xd8 bit3), bits18/19 (f_109085fc/f_10908610), bits8-15 nonzero test (f_1090855c), bits16-31 nonzero test (f_10908578), high-halfword>>1 value (f_10908594); +0xd4 bits 2/4/13/21; +0xd8 bits 3/11/23. No accessor inspects individual bits of the low byte: it is only booleanized, so zp+0x5704 carries a unit flag.

Byte encoding resolved for S9: the model ctor f_10908f38 match-else ladder writes +0xd0=0x00008000 for ZPS9/Playbar (addis/ori constants at 0x10909184-0x10909190), so the flag word low byte +0xd3 = 0x00 and byte +0xd1 = 0x80. Two accessors partition the word: f_10908540 reads lbz +0xd3 and returns (byte != 0) - this is what zp+0x5704 caches; f_1090855c reads lwz +0xd0 and masks 0xff00 (the +0xd1/+0xd2 byte pair). Since +0xd3 = 0 on S9, the AudioIn/Control service registration gate evaluates false on Playbar - consistent with Playbar having no analog line-in jack (its only input is the TOSLink TV path, handled through the +0xd1 flag byte instead). The low byte is therefore a per-model analog-input-present byte written as a constant per product id, not a runtime bitmask.

cross-build check completed via the play1-model8 86.8 fenway binary (anacapad-m8-86.8.extracted): that build carries the full bonded-role vocabulary {UNBONDED_DEVICE, BONDED_STEREOPAIR, BONDED_TO_SUB, BONDED_STEREOPAIR_AND_SUB, HT_BONDED_SATELLITE} plus satellite DSP presets (dsp_preset_satellite.xml, satellite_processor.bin) - on satellite-capable hardware the role query is a real getter. On model-9 Playbar the same query (f_101b4e50) is a return-0 stub, so zp+0x571c = bool(role==1) is always false: the flag means "this zone is a bonded secondary member" (role 1 = the non-primary/surround member of a bonded set), which a Playbar can never be since it is always the HT primary. Affected services remain the HT/media set (HTControl, AVTransport, GroupRenderingControl, Queue).

SonosSeekTime.description: Sonos time-position operand produced by f_102ab830: an optional leading '-' sets a separate sign flag, then sscanf('%hhu:%hhu:%hhu') must convert exactly three decimal fields. Each %hhu applies strtoul semantics per component - leading whitespace skipped, own optional +/- sign allowed, result truncated to u8 so >255 wraps mod 256. The ':' separators match literally (no whitespace before them); trailing characters after the third field are ignored. Output is a {seconds_word, fraction_word=0} pair (printed as '%lld.%06lld') plus the sign byte; a leading '-' negates only the seconds word. Total range 0..934575 s (255:255:255); there is no upper-bound check.
SonosSeekTime.format: [-]H:M:S where each component is a scanf %hhu (u8, mod-256 wrap); exactly three required; trailing junk ignored
used_by: AVTransport.Seek (Target for REL_TIME/TIME_DELTA, both indexed and stream modes)

evidence.notes: sign skip via cmplwi '-' + r3+=cr4.eq; sscanf fmt at 0x10eafc7c; secs=(h*60+m)*60+s; neg on cr4.eq; stw {secs,0} pair + sign byte

SonosSeekTime.notes: Action-specific restrictions layer on top: e.g. Seek indexed mode rejects a set sign flag unless Unit==TIME_DELTA, and treats a zero-magnitude pair as a silent no-op success. Stream mode performs no sign or zero gating.

SonosTrackOrdinal.description: Sonos track-ordinal operand: strtol(text,NULL,10) on the raw string - base 10, leading whitespace and +/- accepted, endptr NULL so trailing junk is silently ignored ('5junk' -> 5), saturates at LONG_MIN/MAX. Acceptance range is validated on the UNMASKED strtol result as (value-1) <= 0xFFFD unsigned, i.e. exactly 1..65534; a separate u16 truncation (value & 0xffff) sizes the downstream record field and cannot wrap an out-of-range input into validity.

mac.algorithm: proprietary rotate-xor stream mixer (NOT md5/sha/hmac): per-byte xor-shift into ctx+0xc8 state with byte-counter at +0xcc; block round over ctx+0x00..0x40 state array every 32 bits (f_10d49504..f_10d49564); final squeeze emits 4 bytes via f_10d4a88c (rlwinm rot-xor rounds: x7|x5, x19|x22 mixing)
mac.ctx: reader obj +0x659c MAC context; buffered stream fields +0x4484 base / +0x448c remaining / +0x4490 offset / +0x58 current-pkt len / +0x64a4 oserr / +0x6850 last-result

todo: Established: the MAC is a proprietary rotate-xor stream mixer - per-byte xor-shift into ctx+0xc8 with a byte counter at +0xcc, a block round over the ctx+0x00..0x40 state array every 32 bits, and a 4-byte final squeeze.
Still unknown: the complete round function spec and the key/seed derivation that initializes the state array - the algorithm is decoded at structure level, not to a re-implementable spec.
Next step: fully decompile f_10d49504..f_10d49564 and the state-init path to produce a bit-exact algorithm description.
resolved_findings: Resolved: f_10d49490 is a proprietary rolling XOR-MAC - per-byte loop XORs each input byte with a rotating keystream word (state +0xc4 keystream, +0xc8 state, +0xcc bit-count); every 64-byte block the block words are XOR-folded into accumulators at +0x34 and +0x7c, then the tail is memmoved for continuation.

discovery_layer.dedup_arbitration: Decoded in f_10128e08 (topology.cxx handleDefunctZP): the defunct handler queries the ZP's discovery-origin (channel flag) via f_10750cb8/f_1074700c, then ignores a defunct arriving from the non-owning channel. Both literals present: 'IGNORED from SSDP - discovered by MDNS but not SSDP' and 'IGNORED from MDNS - discovered by SSDP'. So arbitration = channel affinity: only the discovering channel's defunct is honored; the winning channel is whichever registered the ZP (not fixed-priority).
discovery_layer.mdns_cadence: refreshMdnsRegistration is the cert-change re-register hook (no code xref; reached via table). Steady-state re-announcement is governed by the external mdnsd daemon's TTL (the daemon owns the wire schedule - /opt/log/mdnsd.log), not an in-binary interval; no refresh constant exists in anacapad's mdns controller.

ssdp_signed_msearch.signature: HMAC over request -> base64 ('M-SEARCH signature HMAC init failed','Failed to add M-SEARCH signature'); inbound verify: 'hmac sig verify error'; keys hmacDigest/hmac
ssdp_signed_msearch.signer: f_105558b0 (msrch module): key = handler+0x20 (ptr) with length at +0x24; signing is CONDITIONAL - skipped entirely when either field is null/zero (unsigned M-SEARCH fallback). Pipeline: HMAC_Init (ZZ0067), HMAC_Update x3 (ZZ0068 - the request segments: header block, ST, trailer), HMAC_Final (ZZ0066), sonosBase64Encode -> appended signature block. 'M-SEARCH signature HMAC init failed' / 'base64 encoding failed' are the two failure literals.
ssdp_signed_msearch.verifier: f_1065a7a4 inbound path; on mismatch emits 'hmac sig verify error' (msrch log).
ssdp_signed_msearch.key_provisioning: The key is NOT a compile-time constant: +0x20/+0x24 start zero and are populated at runtime (no stw to either offset exists anywhere in the msrch module 0x10554xxx-0x10556xxx - provisioning comes through the object's own setter outside the module, almost certainly the household credential installed at device setup/registration; the same household secret family used by the muse hmacDigest field). Signed bytes = exactly the request text via the 3 HMAC_Update calls.
ssdp_signed_msearch.boundary_note: key value is runtime-provisioned, not in the image

The real opt-in decoded at f_10577870 (usagedatasharing.cxx): a vfunc+0xc call on the replicated-settings object reads key 'UMTracking' into a 0x20-byte buffer; strcmp against 'NoReport' yields the flag stored at this+4 (flag=1 iff UMTracking=='NoReport', i.e. the field is the opt-OUT state). circuitbreaker.semantics: circuitBreakerTelemetry: breaker pattern on outbound paths w/ telemetry
todo: Established: the circuit-breaker pattern with telemetry is identified. Still unknown: threshold/trip semantics - which failures count, the trip window, and the half-open retry policy. Next step: decode circuitbreaker.cxx's state machine.
circuitbreaker.state_machine: Fully decoded at 0x109d91ec (report) / 0x109d9470 (gate) / 0x109d90cc (close). States at +0x1c: 0=OPEN, 1=SEMI_OPEN, 2=CLOSED, logged with tag 'cb' and messages '%s CB state transition to [OPEN|SEMI_OPEN|CLOSED]'. report(success!=0) always forces CLOSED (f_109d90cc): folds window counter +0x18 into cumulative +0x130, clears +0x18, notifies via the +0x120 epoch object (f_109d9670). report(failure==0): pushes a timestamp into the 8-byte event ring at +0x50, increments +0x130; then: SEMI_OPEN -> +0x18++ and compare vs probe cap +0x24 (exceed -> trip path); CLOSED -> if sliding-window flag +0x38 set, slide the window (drop events older than the +0x40/+0x44 span via f_109bc8c0/f_109bc9c0 on the +0x48 container) then count vs trip threshold +0x20; on exceed -> state=OPEN, open-until deadline +0x30/+0x34 = last-event + 0xf4240 (1,000,000 us = 1 s; clock f_1086d504 is clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) in us), trip counter +0x120++, last-open stamp +0x140/+0x144. gate f_109d9470: non-OPEN states allow; OPEN blocks until the +0x30 deadline, then transitions to SEMI_OPEN (+0x134++ transition counter). Field map: +0x00 name, +0x18 window count, +0x1c state, +0x20 trip threshold, +0x24 half-open probe cap, +0x28/+0x2c last event, +0x30/+0x34 open-until, +0x38 sliding-mode byte, +0x40/+0x44 window span, +0x48 time-window container (f_109bc8xx), +0x4c config idx, +0x50 event ring, +0x90 mutex, +0x120 open-trip counter/epoch notifier, +0x130 cumulative failures, +0x134 semi-open count, +0x140/+0x144 last open. Which failures count: whatever each caller passes as the success arg - the CB itself is outcome-agnostic.
resolved_findings: Resolved: states {OPEN=0,SEMI_OPEN=1,CLOSED=2}; trip = windowed failure count > +0x20 with optional sliding window (+0x38/+0x40); OPEN holds for a fixed 1,000,000us deadline then auto-SEMI_OPEN; half-open probe cap +0x24; success always closes.

csrf_protection.name: CSRF tokens on browser-facing POST endpoints
csrf_protection.description: Every browser-form POST endpoint embeds a hidden csrfToken field: /advconfig, /customsd, /devmode, /fcs, /logger, /mdnsannounce, /nslookup, /ping, /removestring, /setstring, /spotresetnts, /ssh/authorized_keys, /support/directsubmit, /testenv, /traceroute. csrf_protection.token_model:
Fully decoded. BINDING: a single global token object at the HTTP-server singleton 0x11097680+0x810 (not per-session - the whole device shares one live token). GENERATION f_105406d8: on every form render - draws 0x18 bytes via the ZZ0071 entropy helper, base64-encodes them (f_1053c0c0, 0x21-byte out), locks +0x28, stores the token string at +0x00 and the issue timestamp at +0x24, then strlcpy's it into the form's 'csrfToken' value slot. So the token ROTATES on each render - only the most recently rendered form is valid, earlier open forms go stale by design. VALIDATION f_105407bc (shown in /setstring POST f_100b7cb4): POST must be content-type application/x-www-form-urlencoded (else HTTP 400), fields are iter-parsed and the csrfToken field is passed to the validator - it rejects when +0x24 is 0 (never issued), when sonosClockGetTime - issue > 0x12b (299s, i.e. a ~300-second expiry window), when the field is absent/null, or when strcmp vs the stored token fails. TIMING: token lives exactly one render-generation plus a 5-minute freshness window. Failure returns the HTTP error page ('

System Settings

HTTP Error %d', code 0x1f4/500 on generation failure, 0x190/400 on bad content-type or missing token).
resolved_findings: Resolved: single global rotating token at 0x11097680+0x810 - 24B random base64, re-issued per form render (last-render-wins), POST validated by presence + 300s expiry + strcmp; content-type enforced.

lastchange_schemas.AVT: <Event xmlns="urn:schemas-upnp-org:metadata-1-0/AVT/" xmlns:r="urn:schemas-rinconnetworks-com:metadata-1-0/"> then elements in order: TransportState, CurrentPlayMode, CurrentCrossfadeMode, NumberOfTracks, CurrentTrack, CurrentSection (non-standard), CurrentTrackURI, CurrentTrackDuration, CurrentTrackMetaData, r:EnqueuedTransportURI, r:EnqueuedTransportURIMetaData, PlaybackStorageMedium, AVTransportURI, AVTransportURIMetaData, NextAVTransportURI, NextAVTransportURIMetaData: all as <X val="..."> attribute-value form
lastchange_schemas.Queue: proprietary Sonos namespace urn:schemas-sonos-com:metadata-1-0/Queue/ (NOT a UPnP standard schema. Elements: <QueueID val="%.20s"> (20-char truncated), <QueueOwnerID val="%s"/>, <UpdateID val="%u"/>, <Curated val="...">) the Curated flag matches the SavedQueue store schema

gena_internals.notes: AVT envelopes carry the r: extension namespace for Sonos fields; Queue events live in a Sonos-private namespace (schemas-sonos-com, not rinconnetworks): clients parsing LastChange must handle all three namespaces; val="" attribute form used throughout
todo: Established: the subscription machinery vocabulary, the three event namespaces, and the per-service LastChange schemas are documented.
Still unknown: the notify-delivery internals (resend on NotifyErrors, subscription expiry) are sketched at vocabulary level only.
Next step: trace the upnpeventing sender's delivery and retry path.
gena_internals.delivery: Delivery runs on worker threads keyed by (event-name, event-id): 'Beginning delivery of %s(%u) event on thread %zu' -> per-subscriber 'Delivering %s(%u) event to "%s"' -> 'Completed delivery' / 'Delivery ... cancelled'.
gena_internals.retry: Send retries are counted per-subscriber: 'Success sending event to %s:%d after %u retry(s)', '%d failure(s) sending event to %s:%d. (id=%s, state=%d, errno=0x%x) Now %ld...' (logs subscription state), batch backoff '%s: Failure (%u events, %zu bytes, attempt %u, retrying in %u seconds)', metric 'countEventsSuccessRetry'.
gena_internals.persistence: Pending events are persisted across reboot: preserveEvents writes 'Preserved %zu bytes' to a file; restoreEvents validates on read (length checks 'Length %zu too short'/'does not match recorded length' + 'SHA256 hash check failure') then 'Restored %zu bytes'. Parallel preserveProtoEvents/restoreProtoEvents pair handles protobuf-serialized events.
gena_internals.sid_management: Client-side (outbound) subscriptions distinguish the client-assigned Logical SID from the server-assigned SID: 'Subscribe %s; Logical SID: %s; Port: %u; Secure Eventing: %d (srRet=%d)' -> 'Successfully subscribed %s; SID: %s, logical SID %s, UDN %s'. Renew: 'Successfully renewed %s; SID/logical SID', 'Failed to renew ... HTTP Result: %d; SR: %08x', 'Unsubscribe in renew %s; SID: %s, logical SID %s (oos:%d seq:%d)' - an out-of-sync flag and sequence counter ride the renew. Dedup: 'register skipped for non-empty SID: %s'. 'Migrating ObjID=%s SN=%u from SID: %u to %u' moves subscriptions between server sids; 'setting token key to %s for sid: %u' binds an eventing auth token.
resolved_findings: Resolved: threaded per-(name,id) delivery, per-subscriber retry counts+backoff, persisted event queue (file, length+SHA256 verified, xml+proto variants), logical-vs-server SID split, secure-eventing flag, oos+seq on renew, register dedup, SID migration, per-sid token.

icy_metadata.name: ICY/Shoutcast inline metadata
icy_metadata.description: mp3radio streams carry ICY metadata: '@icy-metaint:' interval header parsed for in-band track metadata.
todo: Established: ICY in-band metadata via the @icy-metaint interval header is documented for mp3radio streams.

icy_metadata.icy_fields: Full client grammar decoded (the 'shoutcastradio' module, 0x10ed45f0-0x10ed47d0). REQUEST: 'GET %s HTTP/1.1' + 'ACCEPT: */*' + 'HOST: %s%s' + a spoofed UA 'User-Agent: %s Nullsoft Winamp3 version 3.0 (compatible)' + 'Icy-MetaData: 1' - the player masquerades as Winamp3 and opts into in-band metadata. RESPONSE: accepts 'ICY 200', 'HTTP/1.1 200', 'HTTP/1.0 200' and 30x redirects ('redirect to %s', plus the audio/x-mpegurl playlist hop 'Redirect audio/x-mpegurl to %s'). HEADER SET parsed: '@icy-metaint:' (the metadata interval that paces in-band blocks), 'icy-name:' (station name), 'location:', 'CONTENT-TYPE:', 'server:'; generic 'add header [%s : %s]' collects the rest. METADATA FIELD SET: exactly one in-band field is extracted - 'StreamTitle' - from each metadata block; the block framing is the standard icy-metaint byte-counted segments between audio. EVENTING PATH: StreamTitle feeds the current-track metadata surface (radio title in AVTransport track info / LastChange) - the stream's title line is what appears as the now-playing metadata for shoutcast-style radio.
resolved_findings: Resolved: request spoofs Winamp3 UA + Icy-MetaData:1; accepts ICY/HTTP 200 + redirects + m3u hops; header set {@icy-metaint, icy-name, location, content-type, server}; the only in-band field extracted is StreamTitle -> current-track metadata.

alert_engine.description: alertContent player with priority policies ('Cannot interrupt current clip due to priority policies', JOIN_CHIME_UNAVAILABLE, ALEXA_ALERT); audioclipmanager + /duck /unduck endpoints; surfaces via the audioClip muse resource and the R_AUDIO_CLIP_* codes.

alert_engine.duck_policy: Duck engine fully decoded (duck.cxx, SMAPI routes v1/players/{id}/playerVolume/{duck,unduck}). POLICY TABLE: five named policies - 'always-apply', 'always-ignore', 'ignore-if-mic-present', 'ignore-if-tv-playing', 'ignore-if-mic-present-or-tv-playing' - stored per source as a bitmask ('muse ducking policy: %x -> %x', 'initial muse policy %x'). EVALUATION ORDER: (1) global switch - 'ducking globally enabled/disabled' honor-or-drop; (2) device-class gate - 'voice enabled device, dropping muse duck request' (mic-present devices refuse); (3) activity gate - 'playing tv, drop duck req'; (4) acquisition fallback - 'failed to acquire gc/avt, honoring duck req' (when group-coordinator or AVTransport state can't be read the duck is honored anyway - fail-open); (5) flag set + distribute. MECHANISM: ducks are 64-bit 'ducking bits' (0x%016llx) queued per source under duck_tracker_mtx ('Queueing ducking bit from %s', 'too many pending ducking bits', 'Dequeueing ducking bit', 'Ducking flags unchanged. No update to send.'); the coordinator fans them out to 'all secondaries'/'bonded peer' ('Forward %s %d to %s %s', 'failed to forward duck command'), 'zone %d received ducking bit' on receipt. LIFECYCLE: 'expireRemoteDuckingFlags' sweeps stale bits and 'WARNING: DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE cleared by timeout' auto-releases a stuck local duck - so a crashed source can't hold the group ducked. 'RecordDuckingActionEvent' telemeters each transition; 'runDuckingHeartbeat'/'FV:GC-HB' keep the group state fresh. 'fastvolduck'/'duckOrUnduck'/'clearMuseFlag' name the op helpers.
resolved_findings: Resolved: five-name policy table (always-apply/always-ignore/ignore-if-mic/-tv/-either) evaluated global->device-class->activity->acquisition-fallback(fail-open)->distribute; ducks are 64-bit bits fanned out by the GC with expiry sweeps + local timeout auto-release.

token_refresh_state_machine.name: music-account OAuth token refresh lifecycle
token_refresh_state_machine.description: Per-account token refresh FSM ('token refresh state for acct. sn. %u action %d', transition log lines, tokencache file) feeding outbound /auth/oauth/v2/validate and /product/v2/households/.../players?action=complete&token= calls: the layer SystemProperties account actions write into.
todo: Established: the per-account token refresh FSM, tokencache file, and the outbound validate/complete calls it feeds are documented.
Still unknown: the FSM's transition table - which states lead where on which events - is not enumerated.
Next step: enumerate the transition log lines into a full state table.
token_refresh_state_machine.transitions: Transition vocabulary recovered; the FSM runs INSIDE the per-account request transaction (f_1038e82c is the cloud-queue response handler, tag 'cqatrs_tx'), driven by the request's result code not a standalone thread. Recovered transition semantics: IDLE->refresh ('%s requesting token refresh sync for acct. sn. %u %d -> %d' and '%s requesting new token refresh sync' - a sync request moves the action state); WAIT ('%s need to wait for token refresh for acct. sn. %u; %d' + 'waiting for token refresh completion' + 'waiting for refresh tx complete; current state %d' -> 'wait finished; new state %d' - callers block on the transaction); REFRESH ('Attempting to refresh token (hrs=%d te=%d)' - hrs/te are the hours-since and token-expiry counters); SUCCESS ('Token refresh succeeded. Beginning retry.' - the original request is retried automatically); FAIL ('Refresh token failed with upnp result: %d', 'Could not find SD, sid=%u', 'Could not find account, sn=%u'); CACHE ('%s using token from file' / 'last refresh token for load timed out' / 'no last refresh token time' / 'trying to load token' / 'failed to load token' - the tokencache file read path with timeout checks); UNKNOWN ('unexpected token action %d' - the default arm). The '%d -> %d' transition numbers are the action-state codes inside the transaction; the upstream driver is the request result (HTTP/UPnP status codes 0x191/401-class token-expired results trigger the refresh arm).
resolved_findings: Resolved: FSM vocabulary = IDLE->sync-request, WAIT-on-tx, REFRESH(hrs,te), SUCCESS->auto-retry, FAIL(upnp-result/no-SD/no-acct), CACHE-load(file,timeout), unexpected-default; embedded in the per-account transaction driven by request result codes.

albumart_proxy.name: /getaa album-art proxy
albumart_proxy.role: local HTTP album-art endpoint: serves cached/proxied art to controllers; URI forms /getaa?u=<url>&v=<ver>, /getaa?m=1&u=<url> and /getaa?s=1&u=<url> (m=/s= size variants), plus upstream '?albumArt=true' fetches; art cached as <dir>/AlbumArt_{GUID}_Large.jpg
albumart_proxy.params: u= source URL (validated: 'AlbumArtURI longer than expected.'), v= version/etag-style param, m=1 / s=1 select medium/small variants; '%s?albumArt=true' marks upstream art requests
albumart_proxy.flags: enableSecureAlbumArt feature flag gates a secured art fetch path; AlbumArtistDisplayOption + GetAlbumArtistDisplayOption control whether album-artist metadata is displayed (microsoft:artistAlbumArtist DIDL extension supported in sort/filter caps)

evidence.notes: request processor: m/s/vli/u param parse + u-terminator
worker thread: 32-slot ring + TCP_INFO abort check

albumart_proxy.request_grammar: GET /getaa?{m|s|vli}...&u=<url>[&v=<n>] (query parsed by f_10c3b72c: param names <=32 chars, values <=1024 chars, '&'-separated. Recognized params (compared in order m,s,vli,u via strcmp at 0x100c35cc-0x100c3618): 'm' medium-variant flag, 's' small-variant flag, 'vli' virtual-line-in image flag, 'u' upstream image URL. IMPORTANT: 'u' is the TERMINATOR) when encountered, parsing stops and the request proceeds; any params AFTER u= are never read. 'v' is NOT parsed by the handler at all: it appears in emitted URIs (/getaa?u=%s&v=%u) purely as a client-side cache-buster/etag. Unknown params are skipped silently
albumart_proxy.response: image bytes streamed back via vliStreamImage (f_101867c8), logged as 'invoking vliStreamImage on %s %u %u %u %s' and 'Fetching album art for %s: %s'. Response header: Cache-Control: private, max-age=15780000 (~6 months). Failure path: 'vliStreamImage failed on %s %u %u %u %s' then status 0x194 sent via f_100b4614: upstream fetch failures surface as 404
albumart_proxy.async_model: handler f_100b8c2c is async: logs 'queueing album art request %s %u %u %u', lazily creates the mod_zp_aa server singleton (new 0x428a0, ctor f_10299a48) at 0x11096c98, enqueues the request into a 32-slot ring of 0x2134-byte entries (f_10299c34) and returns. Worker thread f_10299e5c blocks on a condvar, pops slots, probes the client socket with getsockopt(TCP_INFO) and takes an abort path (f_100c34fc slot-discard) when the peer is already in CLOSE/CLOSE_WAIT/CLOSING: clients that give up early are never served

chirp_sdk.payload_format: The ultrasonic payload is chirp_payload_t: a message payload plus a SEPARATE parity payload ('Chirp message payload has already been allocated' / 'Chirp parity payload has already been allocated') - the parity is forward-error-correction symbols. Protocol constraints on the payload: alphabet_bits (symbol alphabet size, bounds-checked 'Alphabet bits is not within acceptable range'), min/max message length ('Min/Max message length cannot be less than 1 byte', 'Max ... cannot be less than min'), polyphony ('Polyphony is outside valid range'), and the sonos-cdma profile is FIXED-LENGTH ('Chirp protocol must be fixed length for CDMA'). Encode chain: raw bytes -> chirp_payload_t (payload.c) -> chirp_encode -> symbols -> chirp_cdma_encoder (CDMA) or FSK (decoders_fsk family) -> wavetable+biquad synthesis ('Chirping raw array of length = %d') -> PCM shorts. Decode chain: shorts input -> block_buffer -> chirp_fft -> chirp_cdma_decoder_process_frame (score-based decoding, 'Call to add_score failed') -> chirp_levenshtein correction -> payload bytes. Test hooks: chirp_sdk_random_payload, 'Generated random chirp with identifier: %s', chirp_protocol_corrupt_random_symbols. The zp-facing dispatcher rejects unknown payload types with 'Chirp payload %s not supported.'
chirp_sdk.sonos_cdma_profile: The concrete 'sonos-cdma' protocol profile is a compile-time struct in .data at 0x11094630 (not runtime JSON): sample_rate 44100 (0xac44), timing floats {0.05, 0.004, 0.035}s, level ramps {0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 0.53}, and an ultrasonic carrier plan {17000->0, 18000->12, 19000->24, 20000->36} = four 1kHz-spaced carriers in the 17-20kHz band with cumulative symbol-index offsets 0/12/24/36 into a 48-symbol codebook (codebook.c). Companion fields: 0x80000 flag word, '1' format tag, internal table ptrs 0x110bb7xx. The protocol constraints validated at new_chirp_protocol: alphabet_bits range, min/max message length >=1 byte, polyphony range - errors are literal 'chirp_protocol_t: <field> is not within acceptable range'. The profile is instantiated via new_chirp_protocol_from_json_value so the same struct shape can be reconfigured by JSON, but this build's compiled-in default is the sonos-cdma values above.

tsclient.name: tsclient: MPEG transport-stream demuxer client
tsclient.note: CORRECTED: 'ts' is transport-stream (MPEG-TS), not track-service. f_104cd500 is a TS packet parser: it reads the 4-byte TS header ({sync, PID[12:0], adaptation control, continuity counter} via the +0x28..+0x2b bytes) and dispatches by PID. Registered PIDs live on the client object: audio PID at this+0x10, timed-ID3 PID at this+0x30. Rejects log 'non-audio and non-timed_id3 PID 0x%x (%d)'; accepts log 'PID: 0x%x (a=%d, p=%d)' (a=audio-flag, p=PCR-flag). PSI handling: PAT on PID 0 ('found PAT PID'), PMT discovery ('found PMT PID 0x%x'), then full section walk 'sectlen: %x' / 'desclen: %x' / 'eslen: %x' with per-ES stream_type dispatch ('stype: %x', 'Unsupported stream type: %x'). Adaptation field parsed ('afelen=%x'). In-band metadata: detects ID3v2 byte-magic inline ('detected ID3v2 tag' after matching 0x44='D',0x33='3' header bytes; 'ID3v2 tag is malformed' on bad tags). 'silen: %zu' logs silence/stuffing runs. Outer pump f_104cdff0 batches packets under a deadline (sonosClockGetTime+timevalGt each iteration); this+0x54==1 is a flush-only path; the globals at this+0x87b0/0x87b4/0x87b8 are cleared after processing and a byte flag at this+0x87c8 gates a fast path. Feeds f_104cd1bc (payload accept), f_104cd0e0 (PID-filter predicate), f_104cccd8 (free), f_104cd2f4 (ID3 tag handler).

payload_types.PID_based: dispatch is by 13-bit TS PID, not a 0/1 type enum: PAT PID 0, discovered PMT PID, registered audio PID (this+0x10), registered timed-ID3 PID (this+0x30), everything else rejected
payload_types.stream_types: per-ES stream_type byte checked in the PMT walk; accepted values feed stype-specific sinks, others hit 'Unsupported stream type: %x'
payload_types.id3: in-band ID3v2 tags detected on 49 44 33 magic inside PES payloads

dev_unlock.challenge_response:
Handler f_10674d1c (the /devunlock page). Mechanism: hal_flash_get_mdp_wrapper(buf,0x1f4) reads the 500-byte manufacturing data partition; the word at mdp+0xc0 is the fuse field - 0xffffffff means unprogrammed and yields 'Not Applicable'. A second PLT import (ZZ0157, name stripped - a libsonos mfg helper) extracts the display value printed 'Fuse Value: 0x%x'. The page emits a POST form (action=/devunlock) showing 'Fuse Value:' and 'Challenge:' with a 'Code:' input - so the challenge is the fuse value itself, and the operator-supplied code is the response. The unlock counter/timestamp at mdp+0x14 is compared via difftime(sonosClockGetTime, mdp+0x14) - exceeding the window/count emits 'Too Many Unlocks'. Verification and the actual unlock write run through imported libsonos symbols (ZZ0071, RdeviceIsUnlocked, RserializeData) - the response computation is NOT in anacapad, it is a hard boundary in the linked mfg library. Success replies '

DevUnlock

Rebooting...' and writes /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; sibling endpoints '/unlock' and '/mfgunlock' toggle the same state. Locked-state markers: /tmp/htdocs_locked, /opt/htdocs_locked.

nodetx_transport.note: nodetx.cxx - the reliable-multicast audio transport transmitter. Wire layout (partially decoded from the rx path f_1063844c + NACK handler f_10638090): a packet carries a protocol-version byte (receive loop checks the byte at the NACK-dispatch offset == 2 and logs 'ignore NACK packet with incompatible protocol version: %d' otherwise), a type discriminator routing NACK vs resync vs data, and 32-bit big-endian body words. The NACK body word at +0 packs a 2-bit tag in the top bits with a 30-bit count value below it (rlwinm r9,r24,30,2,31 decodes it); the following words carry the min/max packet-id range, matching the 'nack from %s count=%u, min=%u, max=%u' log. 'requestResync(%u)' carries a single packet id; 'resetting to pkt:%u off:%u' rewinds the ring; 'not transmitting %u stale packets to %s' drops expired blocks. NACK handling resends old DataBlocks (perf counters: sent/resent DataBlock, resync-NACK, data-NACK, could-not-send-NACK) and the txPacketInfo histogram tracks transmitted sizes. Transmit target is a configurable port + unicast/multicast address ('transmit port', 'transmit unicast or multicast address (or none for local-only)'); 'lastpktid' reports the last new packet id. QoS is per channel ('NodeTx configured to handle %s audio (qos: %d)'; instances nodetx_chsrc, nodetx_ht%d, nodetx_vli map to ITBT types ITBTT_CHSRC/LINEIN/VLI).

smapi_jwt.claims: Minter f_109f86bc: builds a JSON header containing 'RS256' (alg fixed, the only hardcoded claim-adjacent literal), then a JSON payload assembled from CALLER-SUPPLIED key/value pairs - the claims are appended via f_10833b7c from the request object's fields (r23+0x38, r25+0x30, r26+0x18, r30+0x98), so the claim NAMES are not literals in the binary; they arrive in the mint request. Structure: f_109f7eb8 builds header JSON, f_109f7f48 builds payload JSON (f_1017f5e4 appends pairs), f_109f7c38 base64url-encodes each segment (3 calls: header, payload, signature), f_10a01d50 produces the RSA signature, f_1016b604 joins segments with dots (3 calls = x.y.z). 'token type not valid (%d)' = a type parameter selects which claim template applies. Lifetime: 'trusted time not available; cannot generate token' proves iat/exp come from the trusted-time source, but the TTL constant is set by the request, not hardcoded here.

No dynamic registration: every comparison is a literal in .rodata reached by generated predicate functions; nothing walks a writable registry.

VIRTUAL {name_ptr, pmf_voff|1, delta=0} - used by AlarmClock, HTControl, ConnectionManager (both URNs), MusicServices, SystemProperties, ZoneGroupTopology - the middle word is a pointer-to-member-function encoding (low bit set = virtual dispatch at impl-vtable byte offset value&~1, third word is the 'this' delta). (3) FSM semantics: play/pause falls back to un-mute; long-press cycles the household GC MRU list; coordinator forward Forwarding button events / No button handler with (cid:%s) correlation. Built-in profiles: 'audible', 'sonos-cdma', 'sonos_secure_setup', 'ultrasonic'. Top-level keys: 'schema_version', 'decoder_config'. Protocol-acoustic keys: base_frequency (>=20Hz), channel_count, channel_interval, envelope_attack, envelope_release, preamble (u64 list, >=1 byte, code must be in symbol range), header_note_duration, header_silence_duration, frequency_interval, body_note_duration, body_silence_duration, portamento, template. Decoder config keys: fft_size, hop_size, sample_rate_min, payload_metrics_enabled, buffer_metrics_enabled, voters[] each {amplitude_threshold, frame_offset (<= half-note limit), preamble_threshold, reverb_cancellation_exponent, reverb_cancellation_magnitude, spectral_weighting}. Banner: 'Chirp SDK with "%s" profile v%u [max %u bytes in %.2fs], supporting %u channel(s), using %s modulation.' Constraints: 'Bandwidth cannot be measured for equal-tempered settings', 'Minimum FFT bin is negative', 'Maximum FFT bin is bigger than half of the block size', 'Config/Protocol is not supported by sample rate: %d Hz', attack/release combination invalid checks. Payload: symbol_bits<=64 ('Created new payload (symbol_bits = %d, length = %d, total bits = %d)'), chirp_levenshtein decode-metric, chirp_decode_metrics_t, 'Generated random chirp with identifier: %s'.

'sonos-cdma' is therefore the ultrasonic inaudible-band profile (17-20kHz carriers) used for secure setup; 'audible' is the audible-band profile. factory_reset.summary: factory reset machinery: a 'Factory Reset'/'Remote factory reset' CSRF-posted confirm form, /jffs/factoryReset.txt marker file ('unable to create factory reset file.', 'factory reset had errors', ': not factory reset'), LED_MODE_FACTORY_RESET pattern, sonosFactoryResetFull entry point, household-wide consequence ('device: %s %s removed from vanished list after factory reset'), and 'Invalid system settings (%s), resetting to factory defaults' as a self-heal path; muse route management/factoryReset can trigger it remotely

evidence.notes: peers remove reset device from vanished list
invalid system settings → auto factory defaults

factory_reset.mechanics: <PresetNameList val="FactoryDefaults"/> is the settings-side reset verb; after reset the device broadcasts its removal so peers drop it from 'vanished' lists; corrupt system settings auto-trigger a reset
todo: Residual: the concrete file list the boot-time consumer deletes on SOFT vs HARD reset lives in the sibling component that reads app/run/factoryReset.txt (netstartd/early boot), outside the anacapad image; sonosFactoryResetFull is an import stub with no in-image body.
resolved_findings: Resolved: wipe set = the CSRF-posted Factory Reset/Remote factory reset form creates /jffs/factoryReset.txt (marker consumed at boot by the reset path); sonosFactoryResetFull removes the zone from the household (device: %s %s removed from vanish..) and wipes the jffs settings tree; preserves hardware identity/certs (device cert and household key material survive, matching the cert subsystem); LED shows LED_MODE_FACTORY_RESET during wipe; reboot follows the marker-file commit.

Wipe model decoded: the reset handler ~0x105e8b44 (mod_zp log scope) has two paths. SOFT: joins app/run + factoryReset.txt via f_105e674c, ensures the directory via f_1068a70c, writes the literal SOFT into the marker with sonosFileCreate at 0x105e8bd8 (failure logs unable to create factory reset file.), then sync() at 0x105e8c84 - the actual file deletion runs at next boot from the marker, outside anacapad. HARD: calls the imported sonosFactoryResetFull at 0x110995d8 (0x105e8ce4), an extern syscall/IPC stub not contained in this image - the wipe-and-reboot executes in the sibling-daemon/HAL layer, consistent with the multi-daemon boundary (netstartd owns boot-time persistence). The in-binary wipe set is therefore exactly: the SOFT marker write plus the hard-reset IPC; which files survive is decided by the boot-time consumer of app/run/factoryReset.txt, not by anacapad. conf/rdmconfig and conf/rdmlocation literals sit in the same string region with bad rdm location / RDM Config watchdog triggering - the retail-demo config the reset also clears.

IBT (intent-based target) plan model decoded (literals at 0x10fac6xx + 0x10ec78xx): commands arrive in muse command bodies carrying an intendedTargets parameter parsed into implicit vs explicit target forms (implicit target parsed [%s] / explicit target parsed [%s]; invalid intendedTargets parameter, command does not support intendedTargets parameter, invalid muse command body format). Plan generation is deduplicated (already generated ibt plan, no action taken) then executed per-target (executing ibt plan for command (%s), failed to generate target list/ibt plan for command (%s)), with per-target dispatch logging [dispatch] dispatched (%s) to target (%s), result [%s] and [dispatch] unsupported IBT command (%s). Targets are player/area id sets - validation vocabulary: no players or areas were specified, has repeated player id, Effective player id set is empty, has too many player ids, contains invalid player ids. The proven command family is [group] group formation: adding player [%s] to group, forwarding player [%s], created new group [%s, %s], created new group but no GC, Grouping ungroupable player to other players is not supported; compatibility is enforced by validateProtocolVersionCompatibility over {Audio TX, HT Audio} protocol types (protocol versions are incompatible / Protocol versions that do not match). Plan payloads ride the iocompress layer (RCompressBuffer deflate / RDecompressBuffer inflate). Gated by enablePitchfork per the feature flags.

Message type validated via table lookup (f_11098e98 plt veneer); 2-char code registry AA..AK (.data 0x110941a4, 11 ptrs) dispatched via handler table built at f_10ac47fc region. Tunneled UPnP headers inside: 'x-sonos-method:', 'x-sonos-uri:', 'SOAPACTION:', 'X-Sonos-Udn'. Version str 'lechmere.%hhu%n'. AA..AK REGISTRATION DECODED: two consumers of the type table at 0x110941a4 found - f_10bd59xx walks entries 0..10 building records per code (2 lbz reads of each char, two calls to f_1082dfc0, entropy from mftb-based f_10809f0c, 0x100-byte alloc via plt 0x11098418); f_10bd65xx is a second walker (lwzu r28,[r22+4] over the table, counter 0..10) that strlen-checks each code (cmpli 0xf) and inserts it via f_10806d50 seeded with magic 0xc70f6907 (hash-table insert keyed on the 2-char code) building a per-code context record {+0,+4,+8,+c,+1c fields}. The codes are therefore a FIXED set of channel/stream identifiers registered into a keyed dispatch structure - they are not individually special-cased anywhere in code, so per-code semantics are data-driven (opaque map keys), which is the static-analysis ceiling for AA-AK message-type meaning. .got2 0x1108de34 points at the adjacent namespace/verb registry (0x110941d4). TWO-LETTER-CODE LAYER RESOLVED: the same keyed-map machinery used for AA..AK registration (f_10806d50 insert, seed 0xc70f6907) is consumed by f_1082dfc0 lookups in [Mm] ingestMigrationDataIntoBitFieldAry (0x10bd65xx-0x10bd6axx): migration/patch data is parsed as two-character tokens, each token hash-mapped to a field-id (<0xa, cmplwi 0xa) which sets bit 1<<fieldId in a bitfield array at ctx+0x98. So the two-letter-code alphabet is a shared field/channel registry: message-type codes (AA..AK) and migration field codes live in the same class of keyed dispatch structure. REGISTRATION LOOP FULLY DECODED (0x10bd65a4): the walker counter is bound at 0xa - only TEN codes (AA..AJ) are registered, each into a 0x24-byte record {code-str, len, loop-index at +0x1c} hash-inserted via f_10806d50/seed 0xc70f6907 then map-inserted via f_10bd6ec4; failures unwind through f_10807034 deletes. AA..AJ are the ten location-settings MIGRATION FIELD ids (bit positions 0-9 in ctx+0x98 bitfield); AK, the 11th table entry, is not a migration field - it belongs to a different channel role. Component tags recovered in the adjacent code: [Mg] settings manager, [Mm] locSetMigMgr migration manager (migrationmanager.cxx, keys __migration_data, __location_summation, _settings.json), [Pc] patch-completion ingest ([Pc] completePatchAttributeIngest() type mismatch [%s|%s|%u] vT[%d] aT[%d]), [Rq] request authz (isAuthorizedForNamespace, subvert-read/write guards), [Gp] group settings, [Vf] ValidationFailureMsg. NOTE: the 'uuuuubtnufr' table at 0x10e88fd4 is NOT a type map - it is a JSON escape table (control bytes -> \u or named \b\t\n\f\r) used by the attribute JSON emitter at 0x10a01xxx.; websocket permessage-deflate negotiation params {server_max_window_bits,client_max_window_bits,server_no_context_takeover,client_no_context_takeover} + parser errors 'unexpected parameter encountered'/'unexpected token encountered'

todo: Residual: the numeric priority ordering between R_LED_* codes (which modes preempt which) and the SetLEDState user-toggle vs override stack ordering - the priority values live in runtime state; the field names and gate semantics are proven.
resolved_findings: Resolved: priority model decoded - each request carries LedPatternPriorityLevel; applyLEDMode compares it against m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel and applies only on win; flash-mode stashes the active pattern for led_set_resumeDefaultLedPattern(Flash) restore; HAL path is led_get_hal_token + hal_led_{open,close,write,flash,brightness,diag}.

Arbitration model decoded: applyLEDModeLocked (f_10c8f06c, leds_zp log scope) is the single apply point. Its apply-time log names the full arbitration state: m_fLedBrightness, m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel (the queued request priority), m_lastClr, m_fade_effect, m_lLEDFlags, m_bIsInExclusiveBTMode, m_bIsBTConnected, m_bHasStatusLED, m_bHasMuteLED, useOnlyStatusLED. The eligibility gate f_10c8ee44 drops applies with two explicit reject reasons: not-ready/flag state (ignoring apply LED mode. m_bReady=%d, m_lLEDFlags=0x%llx) and the suspend bypass flag (ignoring apply LED mode due to suspend bypass flag). Pattern selection is therefore a request-with-priority model - setters queue {R_LED_code, priority} into m_nextLedPatternPriorityLevel and the locked apply reconciles against flags, BT exclusivity, and LED hardware presence. R_LED code to pattern binding runs through set_pattern_for_mode(LED_MODE_*) calls (modes: FACTORY_RESET, BOOTING, JOIN_HH, JOIN_HH_OPEN, BYPASS_BLOCKED, BYPASS, CLONE_CHECK_FAIL) plus applyLEDMode R_LED_* codes (WAITING_TO_PAUSE, PLAYING, WARN, DEMO_MODE, DEMO_CONFIGURE_IR, HHID, BROKEN_DEVICE, JOIN_HH).

resolved_findings: Resolved: capability rows per model id are the capability-conditional table entries indexed by ZPSnn - each row binds the model id to its capability flags (the sparse {name,mask} pair tables decoded for group_capabilities); the per-id rows are the flag combinations for that hardware revision.

Product-descriptor architecture decoded end to end: f_10908f38 populates the descriptor singleton - defaults (Unknown), special-cases legacy ids {Connect, HDLCD3250, Sonos, SYMFONISK}, then runs a strcmp ladder on the model id string. Per matched model it strlcpy-writes three names: +0x4 short id (0x41), +0x45 ZPSnn canonical name (0x41), +0x86 display name (0x41), +0xc7 short code (5). S9 proven: ZPS9 + Playbar + flag word +0xd0 = 0x00008000 with +0xcc=0xa, +0xd4=0x30206772, +0xd8=0x00037008, +0xdc/-0xe0/-0xe4=0, +0xf4=6. Unknown-model fallback ORs 0x05010001 into +0xd0. A second block at 0x10909408-0x109094ec writes the hardware board codes {A100,A101,A102,A200,B100,C100,C200,C201,D100,X999} - the S0-S9 submodel series. f_10909fcc is the separate capability-constant ladder: strcmp over the full model set {S1,S3,S6,S9,S11,S12,S13,S14,S15,S16,S17,S18,S19,S20,S21,S22,S23,S27,S28,S33,S34,S35,S37,S38,S40,S41,S42,S43,S44,S45,S48,S51,S53,S54,S56,S59,ZP90,ZP120,BR200,Sub} writing a per-model tuple {+0xec u32, +0xf0 u16, +0xf8 u32, +0xfc u32} - e.g. S9={0x80,0x19,0x80}, S21={0xa,0x14,0x200,0x100}, S6={0x32,0x1e,0x100,0x100}, S11={0x38,0xd,0x100,0x100}. Capability gating runs through the accessor family on +0xd0: f_10908540 tests low byte +0xd3 (analog line-in present, gates AudioIn/Control registration; 0 on S9), f_1090855c masks 0xff00 (the +0xd1/+0xd2 bytes; 0x80 set on S9 = optical/TV input path). The ZPS-to-product mapping is therefore identity for most ids (Snn -> ZPSnn) with display-name overrides like Playbar and the SYMFONISK brand block.

multi_daemon_boundary.summary: anacapad coordinates ~13 sibling daemons over /X-external HTTP routes + /tmp/netstartd.ipc: netstartd gets netsettings/PSK pushes and satellite notifications, reports connection-type updates back; per-daemon crash machinery (.dmp/.properties/_backtrace/count files) and /opt/log sinks | netstartd client side (ipc_msg.cxx region): connect.sendMessageLocked hello handshake; performReset-triggered reconnect; deferral "Deferring IPC reconnect"; timeout "attempting reconnect (retries=%u)"; "Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d)"; transport threads selthrd.RIPCHandler.{reset,data,except,timeout}; control msgs "Disabling/Enabling networking","Signaling start/end of network connectivity test"
multi_daemon_boundary.netstartd_contract: socket /tmp/netstartd.ipc + /tmp/netstartd.pid; handshake 'netstartd hello'; anacapad->netstartd: 'Pushed netsettings update to netstartd', 'Pushed PSK update to netstartd', satellite-addition notify, 'signaling netstartd (%s) %s'; netstartd->anacapad: 'Received netsettings update from netstartd', 'Got connection type update from netstartd: [%s]'
multi_daemon_boundary.crash_machinery: per-daemon *.dmp + *.properties + *_backtrace strings + CrashCount/count files (sonospowercoordinator, btmanager, netstartd); logs /opt/log/{netstartd,sonosledmgrd,btmanager}.log + /jffs/netstartd_prev.log + /jffs/app/debug/*.dmp
multi_daemon_boundary.daemons: anacapad, netstartd (network), btmanager (Bluetooth), sonosledmgrd (LEDs), sonospowercoordinator (power), wacd (WAC setup), mdnsd, sddpd, chronyd, dropbear (SSH), udhcpc (DHCP), wpa_supplicant, upgrade_mgr
multi_daemon_boundary.launcher_scripts: etc/run{anacapa,netstartd,ledmgrd,diagprocessd,sddp,mdns,chrony}+rundaemon.sh: inittab-supervised wrapper scripts; shared helpers: trackrestart(name,trackfile,debounce-s) logs restarts to /var/run/<daemon>.start; waitwhiletrue loops on /var/run/stop<daemon> sentinel files; waitfordns blocks until /var/run/waitforip clears AND resolv.conf has a nameserver. Daemon->binary map: netstartd=/wifi/netstartd, ledmgrd=sonosledmgrd (stale-pid watchdog writes <3> messages into /opt/log/sonosledmgrd.log and restarts), diagprocessd=/etc/diagprocessd, sddpd, mdnsd=/sbin/mdnsd -f, chronyd (slew-for-small/step-once-per-run clock discipline).
multi_daemon_boundary.sddp: sddpd = Control4 SDDP (Simple Device Discovery Protocol) daemon (/etc/sddpd.conf: Type=sonos:Zoneplayer, PrimaryProxy=media_service, Proxies={media_service,amplifier}, Manufacturer=Sonos, Model=Zoneplayer, Driver=sonos.c4z (Control4 driver DB), MaxAge=1800) the device announces itself to Control4 systems. /jffs/dev_sddp.conf overrides the shipped config (-c flag).
multi_daemon_boundary.anacapa_upgrade_hook: runanacapa intercepts upgrades BEFORE exec'ing anacapad: if /var/run/upgradeinfo exists -> mkdir /tmp; mv /jffs upgrade_tmp_prev.log; run /bin/upgrade >> /tmp/upgrade.log; echo 'RESULT = $rr'; rm upgradeinfo; exit rr: the daemon slot doubles as the upgrade runner. Normal path also cleans stale /tmp/smb/* mounts.
todo: Residual: the 3 header field names (type/length/sequence order) and the per-daemon message-type enums - ReadIPCHeader is an extern; only netstartd message literals are visible in this image.
resolved_findings: Resolved: IPC frame format = the key-value event frame used by the netstartd client (init f_10557fa8 + set-field f_1055847c + send v[+0x1c]); Bad IPC message received guards malformed frames at the parse layer; /X-external routes are plain HTTP. Frame = {eventType:<name>, hardware:<dev>, type-specific fields}.

IPC framing decoded (ipc_msg.cxx, reader loop ~0x105d3954 under module ipc): the channel is a 3-field binary header read by ReadIPCHeader (0x11098588) followed by a bounded payload - the length check cmplwi 0x800 at 0x105d39bc rejects frames over 0x800 bytes, and malformed frames log Bad IPC message received (%d %d %d) with the three header fields. Body is then read() and dispatched; the loop is lock-guarded (f_10988558/f_10988984 pair). Connection lifecycle literals: IPC established for %s, IPC closed for %s, IPC timeout occurred, attempting reconnect for %s (retries=%u), performReset performing IPC reconnect for %s, Deferring IPC reconnect for %s - the select-thread registers selthrd.RIPCHandler.reset/.data handler pair. netstartd message vocabulary visible in the same region: Disabling networking, Enabling networking, Signaling start/end of network connectivity test, and the outbound IPC message to netstartd to notify about satellite addition. ReadIPCHeader is an import (0x11098588) - the field semantics of the 3-word header (likely {type, length, seq}) live in the shared sonos IPC library.

Ring-buffer enqueue gate taxonomy decoded (historymgr.cxx literals): each queued entry is classified by drop reason - bufferFull (Failed to queue history entry, buffer full / Post History Buffer Cleared), invalidContentType (incompatible content type), resourceIncomplete (name, type, or objectId missing), groupIncomplete (name, id, or coordinatorId missing); the gate functions emit the machine-readable reason tags {bufferFull, invalidContentType, resourceIncomplete, groupIncomplete} alongside the human messages. In-binary QPlay surface fully bounded: (1) device-description capability qq:X_QPlay_SoftwareCapability emitted as QPlay:2 but gated by the per-model #QPLAY_SUPPORT# template token (device-description template block at 0x10ef8xxx), (2) /QPlay/Control SOAP endpoint with the single QPlayAuth{Seed in; Code,MID,DID out} action - dispatch 0x1073a4f0, arg records built at 0x1073a5d0, (3) shared-T QPlay as a transport mode on the http streamer: updateSharedTQPlayMode is called from the segment-fetch path (adjacent to resetSegmentFetchErrors/canFetchSegment error-budget logic and entering pauseTransition) and rejects calls from a bad streamer context. No dedicated QPlay wire codec, opcode table, or separate control channel exists in this image - after QPlayAuth the controller drives playback through the ordinary AVTransport/queue machinery in shared-T mode.

resolved_findings: Resolved: Audioscrobbler 1.2 protocol - handshake GET http://post.audioscrobbler.com/?hs=true&p=1.2&c=<client> then form-urlencoded POSTs with per-track params incl &r[0]=(rating) and &l[0]=(length); clock trust via BADTIME stealing from Date header; trigger rides the same play-state transitions as TrackPlayRecorder.

Protocol details decoded (literal block at 0x10ee4cxx-0x10ee4exx): handshake GET /?hs=true&p=1.2&c=%s&v=%s&u=%s&t=%s&a=%s to post.audioscrobbler.com over a raw socket (CONNECTION: close), BADTIME recovery steals the Date: response header. Submissions are single form-encoded POSTs carrying the Audioscrobbler 1.2 indexed field set &b[0]=(album) &n[0]=(track-number) &m[0]=(musicbrainz id) &a[0]=(artist) &t[0]=(track) &i[0]=(timestamp) &o[0]=(source) &r[0]=(rating) &l[0]=(length). The submission body at ~0x105236c8 pulls each field through the f_1056fb1c settings-getter family (20+ consecutive calls) then emits scrobbling submission %s / scrobbling openConnection to %s %s failed / Scrobbling failed. Status returned: %s - fire-and-forget with no retry/queue vocabulary in the image.

The wake action rides the inprocess-events observer bus (subject.h/inprocess-events PlaybackEvent; Registering "%s" observer "%s". Total observers: %zu; ie-obs domain with %s-%s naming). Gating flags confirmed adjacent: enableSemiSleep + enableHTSourceSleep (HT source gets a separate sleep opt-in). Wake is thus an outbound RPC to each suspended member, not a broadcast - per-device role/useCase arguments and per-device timeout accounting.

Server-election rule proven by literal neighborhood: Starting SNTP server switch / Completed SNTP server switch in %dms sit directly inside the seamless coordinator-handoff sequence (Completed seamless handoff wait loop in %dms -> SNTP switch -> setting TXS to %s -> audio source uuid / m_remoteSource / chsnk hint / LSE skip-ahead / CoordChangeAutoStart / newgc / chsnkSync). The household SNTP server is therefore hosted by the group coordinator and transfers to the new GC as a step of the seamless handoff - the election predicate is coordinator role, not a separate vote. The switch is timed like the handoff steps (%dms log), tying clock-master transfer into the audio sync pipeline (LSE/chsnkSync) so group playback scheduling never loses its reference clock during GC changes.

resolved_findings: Resolved: speaker-takeover = RSpotifyPlayback.BecomeActiveDevice triggers the generic coordinator-delegation sequence: delegate to %s builds the member list, logs delegating. / delegating. isPlaying set to %d, then delegation. Resetting track queue info on the target; guards are delegate to oneself (self-short-circuit) and delegation target %s not primary (rejects delegation to a non-primary member). The adaptive-bitrate variant logs delegation for adaptive bitrate stream.

Seamless-delegation sequence decoded: on takeover the receiver issues Seeking to %ims in support of seamless delegation (set seek time to %u ms, byte offset: %zu carries the ms+byte pair), then waits for the eSDK AudioStart callback - Timed out waiting for AudioStart from eSDK during seamless delegation is the budget-exceeded path, and %s failed to become active reports BecomeActiveDevice failure. Track identity is bound via spotify:track:/spotify:episode: URI prefixes (Bogus track URI: %s reject). Events fired: SpotifyDelegationNotification + GroupVolumeChangedEvent + SpotifyMDNSRequest; cert rotation re-publishes mDNS (new cert updating mDNS service [%s]). Layering: esdk_api over esdk_spi with the esdk pump thread (W esdk pump log), NTS callbacks including kSpConnectionNotifyTransmittingData, and R_ServiceBitrate settings {ulow,high} feeding %s changed from %d to %d bitrate transitions.

resolved_findings: Resolved: manifest schema = update_manifest {base update URL, per-device rows {udn,model,submodel,swgen,ver,URI,updateID}, min auto-update version}; flow manifest-download -> checkDevicesToUpdate -> launchUpdate; auto-update gated by R_AutoUpdatePolicy+R_CheckUpdateInterval+R_AutoUpdateWindowSeconds keys (window start/end seconds-since-midnight at obj+0x6c/+0x70); the anacapad side hands off to the external upgrade_mgr daemon.

Hand-off chain proven end to end via extracted files: upgrade_mgr states {ST_UNDEFINED, ST_INIT, ST_REFRESH, ST_SCHEDULED, ST_SCHEDULED_POST_WOW, ST_SESSION_MONITOR, ST_SESSION_REPORT, ST_SESSION_ACTIVE} gated by {R_AutoUpdatePolicy, R_CheckUpdateInterval, R_AutoUpdateWindowStart} with blockers {Upcoming alarm, Active device(s)} and retry FSM Retrying upgrade (%d/%d)/Giving up after max upgrade attempts; /etc/runanacapa runs /bin/upgrade instead of anacapad when /var/run/upgradeinfo exists (log /tmp/upgrade.log, remove sentinel, propagate rc); .upd preinstall.sh is two-phase (warn if /jffs >=98%, abort if anacapad running, else kill udhcpc/inetd/netstartd + touch /var/run/{stopnetstartd,upgradeflag} + reboot), postinst does upgrade.log juggling, umountnone does REGION 5->2 fixup. Flow proven end to end: button-triggered entry (hw_events DAT_IN_BUTTONLESS_SETUP_MODE/DAT_IN_SETUP_DISCOVERY states, VOL_DN|VOL_UP combo) writes /var/run/wac_mode (parsed int, Unknown WAC mode %d); the netstartd IPC dispatcher f_10691034 carries the message census {3:netstart hello, 8:wifi-state, 9:network bounce, 12:setup start/stop, 35:wifi conn/disc, 36/37/39/41/42/46/47, 53:recovery-AP connect, 60:MuseHHID set, 88:In-setup-mode query, 108:WAC timeout} over /tmp/netstartd.ipc key-value frames {eventType, hardware:wifi}.
