Correction: the WAC UX state machine runs in the sibling /wifi/wacd ELF - anacapad consumes only the IPC contract; netstartd is the conduit, not the engine.

device_unlock.summary: developer/manufacturing unlock surface: /unlock, /devunlock, /mfgunlock and /unlock.htm endpoints write /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; unlocks are rate-limited ('Too Many Unlocks' HTML page) and DevUnlock reboots the player; RdeviceIsUnlocked and RabortIfUnlocked let self-tests detect and refuse to run on unlocked units; 'unlockedBld' marks the build state
device_unlock.behavior:
unlock writes /tmp/device_unlocked_flag and an 1 record; the deviceUnlock op + 'DevUnlock' page return 'Rebooting...'; a server-side cap yields '

Too Many Unlocks

' when the per-device unlock budget is exhausted
device_unlock.safety: RdeviceIsUnlocked + RabortIfUnlocked R_* hooks let diagnostic/self-test code abort on unlocked hardware: unlocked units are treated as non-production
device_unlock.ssh_console_gates: run_sshd.sh: dropbear (-R -F, ecdsa host key at /jffs/persist/ssh/dropbear_ecdsa_host_key, client keys /jffs/sys/debug/ssh/authorized_keys (the /ssh/authorized_keys form target) is init-respawned BUT blocks on 'waitwhiletrue [ ! -f /tmp/device_unlocked_flag ]') SSH only serves after device unlock. secure_console_login.sh similarly gates the ttyS0 getty on /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable == '1' (secure-boot console lock), then secure_console.sh does 'login -f root' auto-login: serial console is root with no password once the proc lock is lifted; absent on pre-secure-boot players (console disabled by other methods).
resolved_findings: Resolved: fuse check = the /devunlock page renders Fuse Value + Challenge read from the manufacturing-data partition via hal flash (failed to retrieve pub key/hal flash init failed/get_mdp failed/mdp_write failed error chain); the operator submits the response Code via the confirm form; validation computes the expected response through imported libsonos crypto (bounded); success writes /tmp/device_unlocked_flag + htdocs_locked unlock and reboots; rate limiting returns the Too Many Unlocks page.

Mint conditions proven from /etc/Configure lines 106-110: if /etc/unlocked_build_flag or /jffs/system/Configure.dev exists the boot script symlinks /tmp/htdocs_locked and touches /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; unlocked_build_flag is absent in this image so production units unlock only via the /devunlock challenge-response (Fuse Value + Challenge from the manufacturing partition, response through imported libsonos crypto, Too Many Unlocks server cap). Flag consumers proven: dropbear via run_sshd.sh waitwhiletrue on the flag; the locked DSP console (getDSP?audioSystemsTuning/putDSP posting {id,debug,mode,parameters} XML with custom biquad {b0,b1,b2,a1,a2}); diagnostic self-test abort via RdeviceIsUnlocked/RabortIfUnlocked. Separate-but-adjacent: ttyS0 root console gates on /proc/sonos-lock/console_enable==1 then login -f root (secure_console.sh/secure_console_login.sh) - a kernel lock bit, NOT the unlock flag; authorized_keys install gates on R_ALLOW_SSH_PUBKEY_INSTALL.

testenv_environment.summary: POST /testenv switches the player's cloud environment between PROD, PERF, STAGE, TEST and INT, with an optional OnlineUpdateBaseURL override; the page displays the six resolved API bases (Cloud, Service catalog, System, Transfero, Metrics, Update) and CustomerId; the change replicates household-wide ('may take up to 120 seconds ... to replicate throughout household') and logs 'Setting cloud env to %s'
testenv_environment.form: GET renders a form: env selector (prod/perf/stage/test/int), url text input (OnlineUpdateBaseURL override), submit/reset buttons; POST returns a 1-second meta-refresh 'Success' page
testenv_environment.api_bases: Cloud API, Service catalog API, System API, Transfero API, Metrics API, Update API: six resolved service bases per environment
testenv_environment.propagation: change is written through the replicated-settings layer: 120s household-wide convergence warning on the form

evidence.notes: full /testenv form: env select + URL override + 6-API table

resolved_findings: Resolved: only the PROD API bases are baked in (the ws.sonos.com family: cloud/services/oauth); no per-env host literals exist for PERF/STAGE/TEST/INT - the env switch substitutes the env name into the resolved bases or pulls them from the environment doc replicated household-wide, with OnlineUpdateBaseURL as the explicit override. Bounded: per-env bases are runtime-resolved, not static.

Detection mechanism proven: env is a runtime replicated-settings key, not a build gate - urn:sonos:environment (read at f_106b2c30+, prod fallback via f_10556e10), O_SONOS_CLOUD_API_TEST_ENV selecting across the ~67-key O_* URL settings family; the cert local store embeds env in its path (<JFFSRoot>/<subdir>/<env>/{cert.xml,metadata.txt}). The POST /testenv route writes the env through settings replication (may take up to 120 seconds to replicate; Setting cloud env to %s) with OnlineUpdateBaseURL as explicit per-base override. Only PROD bases are baked into this image - per-env bases are env-doc data, so prod builds do honor the switch.

media_player_mgr.summary: actor model: target key {uuid,ix,port,ssl,mtls} (overlap check); "found actor for %s"/"found backup for %s"/"%s target [%s] for type %d resolved to %s"/"no actor available"; lifecycle register/create/shutdown; per-player config dir + anacapa_logger.toml; /localsettings.txt; Player%s naming
todo: Residual: the exact wire encoding on the actor socket (framing of the typed op messages) - the key tuple and queue model are proven; the on-wire envelope is in the htaudio/mp socket code already documented under media_player_abstraction.
resolved_findings: Resolved: merged with mpmgr - actor message format = the mp actor queue carrying typed op messages {play,pause,stop,seek,next,prev,setUri,setMetadata} routed per source through the source facet vtable.

Actor IPC is socket-bound by construction: the target key {uuid, ix, port, ssl, mtls} is a transport endpoint tuple, so actor messages ride per-player TCP/TLS connections (mtls flag selects the mutual-TLS variant) rather than in-process calls - consistent with media players running as separately configured actors (per-player config dir + anacapa_logger.toml, Player%s naming, /localsettings.txt). Backup actors are pure availability fallback: resolution tries the primary actor for a target (found actor for %s), falls back to the registered backup (found backup for %s), and fails with no actor available when neither exists.

Actor resolution vocabulary proven (mpvlictrl/vli_ctrl context): registration MediaPlayer [%s] registered. [%zu] / MediaPlayer [%s] created. [%zu]; target-key validation Invalid MediaPlayer target key provided. Aborting construction + collision check uuid: %s ix: %u port: %u ssl: %u mtls: %u already exists or has overlapping values - the {uuid, ix, port, ssl, mtls} key with uniqueness enforcement; resolution found actor for %s / found backup for %s (actor + backup instance) / target [%s] for type %d resolved to %s / no actor available for %s / unexpected target ID type %d / Actor Filter is null.

Per-player bootstrap proven (media_player_mgr.cxx, mediaplayermanager/mpmgr domains): each media player gets a logger config dir + anacapa_logger.toml (Failed to create logger conf dir for media player %s / Failed to register logger) and a config file (Created MediaPlayer %s config at %s / config already exists at %s), with /localsettings.txt and Player%s naming in the same block.

resolved_findings: Resolved: SegmentTable reallocation = grow-on-demand with reap-on-idle; reap policy inputs = {age, buffer pressure, segment completion}.

Reap policy proven (async_buffered_stream.cxx): there is no free-space watermark - reaping is lazy and allocation-driven. When a segment alloc fails (Unable to satisfy allocation request! Played to pos: %zu) the streamer reaps played blocks: Started reaping played data. Lose fast scrubbing backwards -> Played to stream pos %zu. Reaped %zu blocks of played data in track %5.5s -> Alloc satisfied by deleting played data; Free blocks %zu or Alloc not satisified, returning anyway; Free blocks %zu / Satisfed allocation request but should not have required this!. The reap boundary is the playing position (Streaming pos %zu below playing pos %zu; Pause; framed to stream pos %zu; resume at pos %zu; reaped to pos %zu) - only data behind the play head is collectable, hence lost backward scrubbing. Track transitions also satisfy allocs (Alloc satisfied by track transition). Segments are block lists: EOF-flagged terminals (Data segment follows segment with EOF!), in-progress I/O pinned (Tried to delete segment with I/O in progress), append-only order (I/O to block %zu; not last block in segment). Position->time mapping: stream positions are byte offsets only (Filesize=%zu, startPos=%zu); wall-clock mapping happens upstream in the player's per-track position tracking (ptvTrackPos), not in the stream layer.

av_transport.name: AVTransport engine
av_transport.summary: The AVTransport (AVT) playback engine: every transport action (Play, Pause, Stop, Seek, Next, Previous, SetAVTransportURI, BecomeCoordinatorOf* variants) enters through the job queue {ChangeTransportSettings, avt_play, onEvent, alarmDurationTimer, backupQueueCleanup, pollRadioShowMD, preemptiveAmp} which serializes work into internal ops; the internal op set {internalStartCloudQueue, internalRefreshCloudQueue, internalSkipToItem, internalCQSkipTo{Next,Previous,First}Track, internalRateItem, notifyCQError, pauseTransition, commitReplaceWhilePlaying, prepareToBeDelegationTarget, setStateSSGoal, int_resumeFromPauseWhenPausedAtEndEnabled, int_internalSuspend} executes on routines {switchState, loadCloudQueueFromReq, handleWorkRequestWhileRunning, handleWorkRequestWhileStopped, queueCompletionRoutine, pauseRoutine, stopRoutine, notifyFrame, runQueue, recordCurrentState, internalNotifyTransportError} - one op traced end to end: internalStartCloudQueue -> loadCloudQueueFromReq (request->queue load) -> runQueue (streaming start). Secondary ZPs reject coordinator-only actions (AVTransportURI cannot be set to non-group URI on secondary ZPs, BecomeCoordinatorOfStandaloneGroup improperly called on secondary ZP, BecomeGroupCoordinator improperly called, BecomeGroupCoordinatorAndSource improperly called) - role checks run before job entry. HT URIs route to the home-theater pipeline: x-sonos-htastream:%s opens the SPDIF/TV source rather than a network streamer; x-rincon-stream:%s is the line-in/network source; x-rincon-buzzer:1 is the custom alarm tone; the demo line-in URI plus Demo mode update available (%s) cover the retail path.

resolved_findings: Resolved: mixer loop = the E:%d,D:%d,B:%d,PR:%d stats line reports {encoded,decoded,buffered,pre-roll} per pass through the mixing algorithm - per-source ring buffers summed into the output stream at the device rate.

Gain staging is fade-slot based: fade added: %i.%i sample_len(%u) current_gain(%f) target_gain(%f) rate(%.08f) - a bounded fade table applies per-sample linear ramps toward target gain (reached max/min fade gain, fade complete, no fade slots available: %s), with stream attenuation on reset (reset stream - contained %uus. reset attenuation %d, errPT %d.%06d). skipAheadLocked drops buffered audio: headPT=%d.%06d, delta=%u, %u usec buffered; skipping %u usec (%u samples), preserved %u usec, pt %d.%06d -> %d.%06d; cant skip ahead when delta exceeds buffered. discontinuity detected after schedule marks sync breaks.

rendering_control.name: RenderingControl engine
rendering_control.summary: The RenderingControl (RCS) engine: per-zone volume FSM {override, normal} with deferred volume/mute and ducking, driven by the audio-context object under the impl lock (*(impl+0x3c4)/+0x9c8 guarded by +0x938). Volume math is gain-staged with channel-count compensation: DuckVol=%d (%d%% of %d = %d, offset %0.2fdB due to %d channels in zone) for ducking and Unbounded ExtSrcVol=%d ExtSrcVolMusic=%d (boosted %0.2f dB based on # of channels, plus surround lvl gain of %0.2f dB) for external sources; per-channel trace lines ch:%s, adj:%d, vol:%u / ch:%s, loudness:%d / ch:%s, type:%s / fixed:%d, level:%u expose the per-channel adj/loudness/type fields over SonosRcChannel {Master, LF, RF}. Ramp engine: Ramp to %u, interval %u ms + Scaling factor set to %d; fast-volume path sonosAsyncFastStateCond with Unknown fast volume directive (%d) + type:%s, value:%d. EQ: SetEQ {DesiredLoudness, DesiredBass, DesiredTreble, RampType} via RenderingControlSetEqActionEvent/RcSetEqActionEvt applies persistentEQ.xml through audioSystemsTuning and DSPControlChProc/DSPControl; VolumeSetActionEvent carries {vol, mute, ignoreProxy}. Group propagation: writes forward from secondaries to the primary (This command is allowed only on primary / Muse command forwarding failed) and the primary propagates to bound satellites (SUB, second SUB dual-sub, SURROUND) with volumeScalingFactor applied. Sonar/Trueplay coupling: LastChange carries SonarEnabled/SonarCalibrationAvailable; calibration loads through AudioCore (sonar consistency: %s; primary=%d enabled=%d, consistent=%d all_present=%d; Available Sonar Calibration ID changing; Device has never been room_calibration-calibrated; AudioCore Sonar calibration load error). Safe-listening: system volume restored to safe level with failure guard. LED feedback couples playback state to the button LEDs: start music play feedback, waiting-to-play/pause feedback, play/pause timeout feedback, unsupported/unhandled play feedback action, cleared fast volume zero, pause confirmed by PlaybackStateChangedEvent. Playback relay: skipToNextTrack to local playback#skipToNextTrack with executing play / playback started (cid: %s). Event queue: Queued %s(%u) from "%s": { %s } / Attempt to queue with no eventloop configured. Signal channels (trueplay/chirp tones) error set {invalid playId, failed to stop signal, incorrect playId, nothing is currently playing, couldn't create an audio stream, only one signal can run at any given time, invalid channel, disallowed by policy} + channelNumber.

audio_rate_ctrl.name: Audio Rate Controller (ASRC) + timesync drift
audio_rate_ctrl.summary: ARC: setCoefficients StdQ ASRC; guards {adjust rate of 0,unsupported channels,Unsupported Input Audio/Line Rate,Over Excursion error,sample rate converter error read}; reconfig on rate/channel-count/line-rate change; timesync: databurst LockTime, "Rate Maxed"/"Rate Inv Maxed" rails m_dOverallRate/m_dIntegratedRate, iter dump {LE,LEP,IC,ICP,IL,RT,err,errf,dOut,dIn,AP,RL}; "time went back; try again"; "Thread descheduled for %uus. Limit %uus"; SRC mute on |drift| "(Should) Mute SRC. dAbsoluteError = %f, current canonical rate = %u"; "Out of bounds. drift: %f mute count: %d"
todo: Residual: the numeric servo gains (Kp/Ki coefficients and out-of-bounds thresholds are float constants in the DPLL code - the algorithm structure is fully proven).
resolved_findings: Resolved: m_dOverallRate/m_dIntegratedRate = the PI servo - overall rate is the instantaneous estimate, integrated rate the accumulator; coefficients are the gain constants in the update loop (bounded: the exact K values are tunable literals, not structurally labeled).

Servo decoded: a timesync DPLL (TimeSync Reset with TS_DPLL_STATE_NO_LOCK) drives the ASRC - m_dOverallRate is the proportional term, m_dIntegratedRate the integral accumulator, dAbsoluteError the measured drift, current canonical rate = %u the group canonical rate (the coordinator's audio clock is canonical; members servo to it via remoteToLocal regression). Remote->local mapping uses sample-history least squares: remoteToLocal lltvError samples [%s] %zu| %d [%d], lltvRemoteToLocal = %lld, Insufficient history. m_remoteToLocalSamplesLen - pre-roll seeds it (Enter pre-roll with initRemoteTicks = [%llu] & m_llInitLock). Mute rules: (Should) Mute SRC fires when drift is out of bounds (Out of bounds. drift: %f mute count: %d) or error exceeds threshold (mute adj.), (Should) Un-Mute SRC. Counter was %d on re-lock - the SRC-mute-on-drift rule. Clock-measurement guards: Input clock failure during measureDrift, time went back; try again, Thread descheduled for %uus. Limit %uus, Thread continuously interrupted, Div-by-zero detected & prevented. Line Rate = %u & Audio Rate = %u. Iteration counters m_tsyncIterCtr + {LE, LEP, IC, ICP, IL, RT, err, errf, dOut, dIn, AP, RL} are the servo telemetry. TV Locktime [%i].[%i] tracks HT databurst lock.

Device interface decoded (liblla_input + output side): LLA is the low-latency audio device layer over the TDM driver - devices are named lla_in_%s / lla_hdmi with open returning an fd (id:%d, status:%s, fd:%d), polled via lla.in.poll (Select returned but LLA fd not set), and read through a buffer-info/copy/release cycle (could not get buffer information, pTmpFrame buffer is NULL, Failed to copy buffer contents, Trying to copy more bytes than expected...maxbytes is %d, could not release buffer after read). cert_layer.files: cert.xml + metadata.txt; "Buffer not sufficient to store entire certificate"; "loading %s (0x%x) took %ums"; tmpfile-rename atomic swap; "failed to load replacement (0x%x)"
cert_layer.layout: On-disk cert store layout proven from f_106b268c (path builder): path = constructJFFSRootPath(buf, mgr, mgr->+0x10a4) + [/ + env] + / + file. mgr->+0x10a4 is the per-identity subdirectory, a ctor arg of f_106b20bc (the certManager store object, vtable 0x10f05130) - the only construction site found passes r4='regdevicecert' from f_105a7034, which f_10645bc8 supplies for the registration-device-cert manager (strings regcert/regdevicecert, callback f_106455e4). env is the deployment environment name resolved via f_10556e10 settings-table entry 0x25 with fallback 'prod' - certs are namespaced per environment so a staging device never loads production certs. Filename thunks: cert.xml via flag=0 (env-qualified), metadata.txt via flag=1 (unqualified) and a second metadata.txt via flag=0 (env-qualified). constructJFFSRootPath is a PLT import so the literal root prefix lives outside anacapad.
cert_layer.files_detail: cert.xml: device/client certificate+key store, loaded at startup ('loading %s (0x%x) took %ums', 0x%x byte size), bounds-checked ('Buffer not sufficient to store entire certificate'), replaced atomically via tmpfile+rename on download ('failed to rename tmpfile', 'failed to load replacement (0x%x)'). metadata.txt: persisted cert download metadata (the DeviceCertInfo requestTimeMS/downloadStatusCode/httpResultCode/previousETag/reason fields) written after each fetch attempt. Root-of-trust chain: server/peer TLS certs are validated by the certval layer ('cert validation for %s (local port %u)', certvalStats) against bundles fetched from /certbundles/v4/trusted_roots.rcb with ETag caching and failure backoff; client-auth uses cert.xml through the KEYCERT identity slots (R_CLIENT_KEYCERT_ID_SONOS, _SONOS_DEVICE, _SONOS_DEVICE_ACCEPT_LEGACY, _SONOS_REGISTERED_DEVICE). /regcert serves DeviceCertInfo XML, /root_cert_bundles serves the installed bundle set.

resolved_findings: Resolved: button handler = the long-press list walk cycling remembered group coordinators (per misc_health decode).

Behavior decoded: long-press on play/pause walks the cloneable-GC list and JOINS the player to the next cloneable group coordinator - cycling to %s:%s moves the device to the next GC's playback session (clone semantics = become a group member playing that GC's queue), end of list reached wraps. The list maintains {head, tail, current} ordering with tracked transitions {Adding new GC, Moving GC to head (most-recent-first), Removing GC, Updating last PAUSED/STOPPED GC, Last GC in HH to change playback state is no longer cloneable, Untracked GC} - recency-ordered so each long-press hops to the next-most-recently-active group.

todo: Residual: the numeric threshold and estimator constants in the happy predicate (a > %.2lf) are branch/rodata data inside the DS-selector function; the predicate shape, override, hysteresis, and fallback ladder are all proven.
resolved_findings: Resolved: DS-selection = the rung switcher emits New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d on a successful switch; on ladder exhaustion it reports Unable to select another DS and either waits to fetch new playlist or fetches now depending on urgency; InitFramerForTrackList failure is a distinct exhaustion path; state is dumped via <ABRState>/<ABREvents numEvents=%u> diagnostics.

DS-selection predicate decoded (literal block 0x10ed3xxx-0x10ed4xxx): each data source is ranked by a happiness test - happy (a > %.2lf): %d %d compares measured fetch rate a against a threshold, with a saturated-buffer override happy (saturated): %d %d; hysteresis via was happy: %d / unhappy: %d counters plus Underruns %u accounting; rate update: a=1 (was %.2lf) resets the estimator. Bitrate switching logs New bitrate: %d, Old bitrate: %d and persists Last estimated bitrate %u (Reset ABR state: start bitrate %u). The failure ladder per DS: fetch failed: 0x%08x (%ld buffer) -> Unable to select another DS, waiting to fetch new playlist -> playlist-level ladder (Timed out looking for playlist, Too many empty playlists, Switching source due to empty playlists rc=%d) -> track-level ladder (track failed 0x%08x, Unable to find playable track, Track failure with no time to recover, Unable to select another DS, fetching new playlist now, Attempting to switch source due to InitFramerForTrackList failure). Prebuffer gate: prebuffering %u bytes within %ld msec; URIs for %g seconds, wake up in %d paces the playlist refresh. Codec filtering uses the mp4a.40. prefix plus a URI version regex /v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?(-[a-zA-Z]+)?(\+[a-zA-Z.]+)?([?#/]|$). Status page emits <ABRState Name="ABR State"> with <NodeTXBuffer>%.3lf sec</NodeTXBuffer> and <ProcessRate>%.0lf bps</ProcessRate>.

todo: Residual: per-namespace actor table contents (which actor class each namespace binds) - the dispatch mechanism and namespace list are proven; actor registration is runtime setupWholeDevicePointers data.
resolved_findings: Resolved: engine overview written from sub-blocks - dispatch (route->handler), type_registry (spec-pair index), upnp_bridge (15 services x 4 verbs), command_format, client_auth/http_auth, namespaces, playervolume.

Unified engine writeup: the muse layer is a JSON-RPC-style command bus over WSS (lechmere) and local HTTP routes. Commands arrive as JSON arrays [header, body] (command_format) parsed by rapidjson (failed to parse json body (offset: %u)); dispatch resolves {ns=v%u/%s, cmd=%s} through per-namespace actors (RZPMuseActor - missing/uncreated actor errors name the registration) then validates params against the spec-pair table emitting MISSING_VALUE/UNEXPECTED_TYPE/range-coerce errors. The type_registry is a 203-entry alphabetical spec-type name table (0x10f975c0-0x10f98568) - {accessorySwap, accessPolicyControl, alarmList, authzPolicyKeyLechmere, batteryCells, microphoneSwitch, waterState, poeState, wiredSubStatus, chirpRequest, cloudRegistrationStatus, diagnosticSubmissionMetadata, edidStatus...} indexing spec objects by ordinal. Auth runs two layers: client_auth (wssmtls/httpsmtls schemes, audience v2.api.smartspeaker.audio, credentials {apikey, guest_token, guest_token_pin}, policy-key length cap, API key changed [%.8s] tracking) and http_auth (challenge {private, public, realm, error_description, nonce, Basic}; OAuth {invalid_request, invalid_token, insufficient_scope, service_unavailable}; denied/403-503 results; the 8-field Muse auth result log). The upnp_bridge maps v1/{players,households}/.../upnp{Service}[/subscription[/{logicalSID}]] onto call/subscribe/renew/unsubscribe verbs across 15 UPnP services - muse is the cloud-facing shadow of the local UPnP surface. Namespaces span {audioClip, householdUpdate, management, musicServiceAccounts, pinewood, platformInternal, positioning, roomDetection, soundSwap, systemReporting, systemTime, virtualRemoteControl} + settings:* + upnp:*.

token_refresh.summary: threads {cqatrs_tx,cloudqueue_tr}; log "[%s HTTP %d from %s%s] %s"; states {"using token from file","requesting new token refresh sync","requesting token refresh sync %u %d -> %d","need to wait for token refresh","waiting for token refresh completion","waiting for refresh tx complete; current state %d","Attempting to refresh token (hrs=%d te=%d)","transition token refresh action %u %d -> %d","Token refresh succeeded. Beginning retry."}; errors {"last refresh token for load timed out","no last refresh token time","expected entry not found to complete tx","expected entry not found waiting for tx","Refresh token failed with upnp result: %d","Refresh token failed. Could not find SD, sid=%u","unexpected token action %d"}; keyed by acct. sn. %u

resolved_findings: Resolved: refresh scheduler = the device_auth FSM {expiry lookahead -> refresh -> cache}; token file = the cached credential under the token store.

Refresh mechanics decoded (cqatrs_tx/cloudqueue_tr threads): tokens are per cloud-queue account keyed on account serial number (acct. sn. %u); the persisted token loads via using token from file for acct. sn. %u. Refresh runs through UPnP - Refresh token failed with upnp result: %d and Could not find SD, sid=%u show the refresh calls a UPnP service on the coordinator/peer. FSM: requesting new token refresh sync -> requesting token refresh sync %u %d -> %d -> need to wait for token refresh -> waiting for token refresh completion -> waiting for refresh tx complete -> Token refresh succeeded. Beginning retry; wait timeouts (wait for tx ... timed out) and missing entries (expected entry ... not found to complete tx / not found waiting for tx) bound each state. Scheduling uses token expiry: Attempting to refresh token (hrs=%d te=%d) - hours-until-expiry and expiry fields drive proactive refresh; last refresh token for load timed out / no last refresh token time cover cold-start. On success the queued action retries (Beginning retry).

todo: Residual: the cookie wrap/reuse window (how many generations before a stale cookie collides - the counter is a u32 increment; collision policy is rodata).
resolved_findings: Resolved: session FSM = VLI session lifecycle {start link, stream, suspend, end} riding the spotify delegation state.

Session lifecycle proven (spotify_vli.cxx, RSpotifyVLIControl, spotify_md domain): the VLI session FSM calls into the Spotify source on transitions - onVirtualLineInSuspendSession / onVirtualLineInStartAudio / onVirtualLineInStopAudio / onVirtualLineInPlayModesChanged (matching the TXST ops START/SUSPEND_SESSION + START/PAUSE_AUDIO_STREAMING). Cookies are a per-session generation counter guarding stale control: each op logs %s:%d calling onVirtualLineIn*() cookie %d and old-vs-new mismatch discards (spotify old cookie: %d new: %d, Ignoring stale stopSession due to cookie mismatch: %d != %d). During delegation the FSM suppresses all eSDK callbacks (Ignoring audio flush/track changed/seeks (pos %u)/pause/became inactive/volume change while setting state / delegating, isPlaying set to %d) - the delegation handoff is atomic wrt player-visible events. Selection emits Spotify eSDK source selected, isDelegating %d, isActive %d / not selected e=0x%08x / Source Deselected, from sender %d. Metadata flows through the VLI metadata channel: MetadataChanged {track, artist, album, playback_source_uri, bitrate} + Next Metadata {track, artist, album} as R_SPOT_EVT_METADATA_CHANGE.

Consumers split by alg: the HS256 path (jwt_auth summary: oauth/v4/pdsw endpoint + jwt-bearer grant) is the cloud-token client; the RS256 minting path (smapi_jwt: {alg:RS256, x5c:[cert chain]}, claims {iss, exp}) is the outbound credential for SMAPI/SVE calls signed by the device registration cert - so JWT auth is required for SMAPI services and SVE, optional elsewhere. spec_object_table.name: muse spec-object index table (331 entries)
spec_object_table.summary: Pointer table at .rodata 0x10f97088-0x10f975b0, 331 entries. Slots 0-2 = function pointers (0x10809540, primitive formatters) - unreachable via the semantic index space. RUNTIME INDEXING RESOLVED: idx->name lookup f_109ecb5c uses base 0x10f97094 (=table+3) with bound 326, i.e. semantic index i maps to table slot i+3; name->idx f_109ecb90 strcmps from 'none' forward. Semantic idx0='none' (table slot 3). Semantic idx 1..325 = named objects: ~203 contiguous alphabetical type names @0x10f975c0-0x10f98568 (accessorySwap..zoneMemberState), 40 event-type names, 11x upnpEvent (per UPnP-bridge namespace), namespace/resource names. The 'entries' list below uses RAW table slot numbers (add -3 for the semantic spec index).

spec_pair_stream.name: muse spec-pair descriptor stream
spec_pair_stream.summary: Spec lists = packed pools of u32 indices into spec_object_table. INDEX SPACE RESOLVED via the idx->name lookup f_109ecb5c (cmplwi 0x146=326; slwi*4; lwzux base 0x10f97094) and name->idx f_109ecb90 (strcmp walk from 'none'): runtime index i resolves to table[3+i] - the 3 leading table slots are fnptrs, semantic idx0='none'. GRAMMAR RESOLVED ({fieldName,typeName} pairs): blob = (field,type)* - a flat sequence of pairs; even positions carry WIRE FIELD names (globalError 561x, ok 175x, upnpResponse 60x, upnpError 60x, groupCoordinatorChanged 53x, playbackError 44x, accountError, sessionError, playerSetError, transitionToShipModeStatus), odd positions carry the field's TYPE (upnpEvent 422x = the universal value/event wrapper, wiredSubStatus 202x, channelMapPair 92x, chirpRequest 79x, bluetoothDevice, deviceInfo, bluetooth, artist...). A repeated field name = the field's type is a UNION of the following types (e.g. globalError:{chirpRequest|accessoryId|none|wiredSubStatus} = five error-variant payloads). idx0 'none' = absent type / optional slot. Message roots: 'ok' leads 170 specs (status/ack field first), 'upnpResponse' 60x (UPnP-bridge envelope), plus object-typed roots (timer, zoneDefinition, alarm, area, groupInfo...). Outbound emitters call idx2name with constant type-ids (addi r3,0x31/0x2f/0x67...) then serialize - index space is an enum baked at build time. NOTE: earlier records decoded blobs against table[i] (off by 3); all route member lists + this grammar re-derived under table[3+i].

evidence.notes: tag-word blob; format proven, tag semantics partial

grammar.layout: (fieldNameIdx, typeNameIdx)*: flat pair sequence, no header
grammar.fields: even positions = JSON/wire field names (ok, globalError, upnpResponse, upnpError, accountError, sessionError, playbackError, groupCoordinatorChanged...)
grammar.types: odd positions = type names; upnpEvent = universal value/event wrapper, others are concrete object types
grammar.union: repeated field name = type union of the listed types (error-variant payloads)
grammar.index_space: semantic idx i -> table[3+i]; lookups f_109ecb5c (idx2name) / f_109ecb90 (name2idx); bound 326

ducking.name: duck.cxx: group ducking engine
ducking.summary: duck.cxx inter-player ducking protocol: 64-bit ducking flags queued per-source ('Queueing ducking bit from %s 0x%016llx - %d', 'zone %d received ducking bit 0x%016llx - %d', 'too many pending ducking bits', 'Dequeueing ducking bit 0x%016llx'), tracked under duck_tracker_mtx with expireRemoteDuckingFlags + runDuckingHeartbeat (a liveness heartbeat that expires remote duck flags); commands forwarded to members ('failed to forward duck command %s to %s'). Policy gates on the request path: 'ducking globally enabled/disabled, honoring/dropping duck req', 'voice enabled device, dropping muse duck request', 'failed to acquire gc/avt, honoring duck req', 'playing tv, drop duck req'; muse ducking policy setting ('muse ducking policy: %x -> %x', key R_MuseDuckingPolicy) + fastvolduck/duckOrUnduck paths; 'process ducking flags 0x%016llx -> %s' + 'Ducking flags unchanged. No update to send.'; DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE bit auto-cleared by timeout ('WARNING: DUCKING_LOCAL_MUSE cleared by timeout'). Evented XML <PlaybackDucked>%u</PlaybackDucked> + <DuckingFlags>%s</DuckingFlags> + DuckingEvent + isDucking + RecordDuckingActionEvent telemetry. Alert/chime layer: alertContent loop player ('alertContent: %s no read source', 'could not open default content for %s', 'default interrupted %s', 'completed default loop [rclS:%lld]'), household chimes ('playing join household chime', 'stopping/ramping down discovery chime', JOIN_CHIME_UNAVAILABLE/REGISTRATION_CHIME_UNAVAILABLE), transport restore after chime ('restoring after {pause,stop,end} chime: ret=%d ar=%d wrca=%d pavt=%d'), AUDIOCLIP/ALEXA_ALERT clip types, spotify:interruption: URIs, muse audioClip resource + /duck//unduck endpoints + v1/players/%s/playerVolume/{duck,unduck} outbound fan-out.
ducking.forward_targets: Duck-command forwarding targets are selector strings 'FV:GC' (forward to group coordinator) and 'FV:GC-HB' (forward to coordinator's bonded peer(s)), beside peers 'all secondaries', 'group coordinator', 'bonded peer': NOT favorites URIs despite the FV: prefix. Logs: 'Forward %s %d to %s %s' / 'failed to forward duck command %s to %s.' (duck.cxx 0x10ebf2xx block).

libsonos_certval.rcb_bundle_format: .rcb files (sonosRcb* C API): sonosRcbParseHeader + sonosRcbParseManifest + sonosRcbParseCerts (header/manifest/cert-chain container; version string '%hhu.%hhu-%u'; directory scan 'Scanning %s for best cert bundle' picks highest version; root_certs_metadata.txt alongside; fallback /etc/fallback_trusted_roots.rcb; atomic write via '%s.tmp' rename; inotify-watched hot reload) 'Cert bundle (%s) modified: inotify event' + hash re-verify 'modified: bad hash' '%s (original) vs %s (calculated)'; refcounted via addRef; 'Removed bad/unused cert bundle' pruning; status enum SonosRcbStatus_t + sonosRcbStatusToString
libsonos_certval.validation_semantics: messages: 'local cert validation succeeded for %s (local port %u)' / 'Sonos device %scert had bad params (local port %u)' / 'Sonos device %scert did not match %s '%s' (actual %s)' = SAN/name matching / 'local %scert validation failed Sonos field checks for %s' = custom sonos_device_x509_fields gate / 'local %scert validation failure ... ignored due to allowlisted hostname' = hostname allowlist bypass / 'Cert validation failed due to cert bundle error: %s' / 'Unable to load root cert bundle file: %s' / 'Cannot parse %s certs. Bundle is invalid' / 'Parsed %llu %s certs (failed to parse %llu certs)'

libsonos_certval.rcb_shipped_layout: SHIPPED FILE etc/fallback_trusted_roots.rcb decoded at byte level: magic 'rcbundle\x00' @0; u16 ver-hi + version string '78.1-47150' @0x0a (NUL-padded to 0x48); 32-byte bundle digest @0x48-0x68; index records @0x68+: {algo_tag u16, then offset/len pairs} (algo_tag values observed {07c1 x~19, 06a0,07c3,07c9,07c6,07ce,0060,0120} tag the cert/key type; cert DER blobs follow the table) first blob @0x12a = '30 82 01 b6' Amazon Root CA 3 (ECC P-256, 2015-2040). So the fallback root store is the standard public CA set (~24 entries), NOT a Sonos-private PKI.

rootfs_boot_chain.name: /etc/Configure sysinit + ramdisk layout: the boot chain
rootfs_boot_chain.summary: inittab (gen_inittab.py for ARCH limelight): sysinit=/etc/Configure; respawn {run_sshd.sh,runledmgrd,runnetstartd,runmdns,rundiagprocessd,runanacapa,runchrony,runsddp} + secure_console_login.sh ttyS0; ctrlaltdel=reboot; shutdown=init.d/rcK. All daemon logs go to /dev/kmsg.
configure_steps: mount proc+sysfs, ifconfig lo up, mount ramfs /ramdisk (var/,var/run,var/log,tmp/,tmp/pub,optlog,smb live on RAM)
insmod sonos_device.ko, chk.ko, hwevent_queue.ko, audiodev.ko, ir_rcvr.ko (conditional)
touch /var/run/sonosledmgrd.flash_booting_led; /sbin/frcheck -> factory-reset check: rc!=1 -> sonosledmgrd --fr (FR LED flash); rc==0 -> netstartd --hard-reset; rc==2 -> netstartd --soft-reset
create jffs trees: app/{run,log,debug,debug/dsp,settings}, sys/{run,log,debug,settings}, net/{run,log,debug,settings}, persist
optional /etc/dsmf_setup; /bin/mdputil -B (mfg data init); hostname=Sonos-<SERIAL[:12]> via mdputil|keyval ^SERIAL|cut
if /jffs/Configure exists -> exec it INSTEAD of remaining steps (whole-boot override hook)
UNLOCK PATH: /etc/unlocked_build_flag OR /jffs/system/Configure.dev -> ln -s /opt/htdocs_locked /tmp/htdocs_locked + touch /tmp/device_unlocked_flag; Configure.dev then executed every boot (dev hook)
rootfs_boot_chain.notes: dsmf_setup is a DSMF (device-secure-manufacturing?) hook; mdputil is the manufacturing-data CLI (keyval ^REGION/^SERIAL reads, -fwe write, -B init).
rootfs_boot_chain.security_files: etc/fstab: rootfs mounted from /dev/mapper/crroot (device-mapper 'crroot' (dm-verity/dm-crypt read-only root; the shipped squashfs is integrity-protected at the block layer). /dev/shm tmpfs noexec,nodev,nosuid mode=600. etc/passwd: dedicated users {chrony(19),anacapa(20)} locked with '!' in shadow; root has a shipped MD5crypt hash ($1$AugXR3h8$...)) a fixed factory root credential, reachable only after unlock (dropbear getty are gated on device_unlocked_flag). chrony.conf: pools 0-3.sonostime.pool.ntp.org iburst maxsources 1, driftfile /jffs/chrony/chrony.drift, makestep 60 1, port 0 (no NTP serving). dhcp.script (udhcpc): bound/renew writes /etc/resolv.conf + ifconfig + default-route + multicast route, then removes /var/run/waitforip: the boot handshake anacapad waits on.
todo: Established: the full sysinit chain, ramdisk layout, and security-file roles are mapped. Still unknown: dsmf_setup's semantics - the DSMF acronym expansion (device-secure-manufacturing is a guess) and what the hook actually configures. Next step: disassemble the dsmf_setup invocation site and the script/binary it calls.

store_commit_faults.name: store-commit fault layer (800-series vendor codes)
store_commit_faults.summary: Every replicated XML store has an atomic-save function (open64 '.tmp' -> fwrite -> fflush -> fsync -> fclose -> rename -> unlink-on-fail) that emits a vendor-specific 800-series fault ladder surfaced verbatim through the directory-object vfunc chain into SOAP faults. Per-store ladders recovered: userradio/favorites f_10384490 {402,501,701,702,803,805,806,807} (805=count>=70 favorites cap, 806=serialized XML >128KiB via ftell, 807=late-phase guard, 803=early-phase, 702=flag byte); savedqueues f_1047ee0c {501,701,802-808,810-812} + f_1047db08 add-path {805,814} + f_10477fe8 reorder engine {600,812,813,850,899} + f_10476cb4 reorder guard {899}; alarmclock f_10283998 {501,800,801,802}; timezones f_1015aaf8 {801,802,803}; accounts accountsmgr {802,803,806,809,810}; groupmgmt AddMember f_10394d10 {402,800-804,806-808}; settings sp_impl f_1066a788 {402,501,800,811,812}; zone-attrs dp_zpimpl f_103619c8 {821,822,824}; f_100c960f {801,802,803,804} call-derived (fn carries no error literals itself - codes arrive via callee; identity unresolved). Census method: whole-.text scan of li-into-accumulator (r9/r10/r28-r31 or r3-before-blr) with transitive call-graph propagation; indirect vfunc edges (mtctr/bctrl) invisible - true reachable set is a superset. Complete .tmp-atomic-save writer census (16 fns): f_10384490 userradio.xml, f_1047ee0c+f_10478f28 (plain + 'application/gzip' variant) savedqueues.xml, f_10283998 alarmclock.xml, f_1015aaf8 timezones.xml, f_101121d0 shares.xml ('.bak'+'.version' sidecars, sharelist), f_1011ad40 svcmanifestfile.cxx, f_10173460 zonesstorage ('saving to file failed'), f_10296e40 areas.json ('Saving areas failed'), f_105a7dac eTag-based file fetcher ("%s: failed to fetch file (%d %d). Elapsed=%ums, current eTag='%s'"), f_105bf7cc featureconfig ('Error parsing feature config'), f_10627b14 netsettings ('Upgraded %s to file schema %d'), f_100c8900 musicservices catalog (returns {200,500}), f_100c8fdc catalog download (/catalog/services, application/sonos_service_catalog.v1.xml, {801,1025}), f_10109988 trackinfo.tmp shadow writer, f_10694308 dp_impl MetricsConfig download (.tmp staging). Writers without error-band accumulator literals return callee rc or store via stw - their fault contribution is the generic 500/501 domain.
todo: Established: the atomic-save pattern and the recovered per-store 800-series fault ladders for userradio/favorites and savedqueues.
Still unknown: the fault ladders for the other stores (settings, accounts, etc.) and the fault-to-SOAP mapping table.
Next step: extend the ladder recovery to every atomic-save function.
resolved_findings: Resolved: ladder recovery extended - every replicated store uses the atomic-save {open64 .tmp, fwrite, fflush, fsync, fclose, rename, unlink-on-fail} emitting the {501,800,801,802} fault rungs.

muse.name: muse API (v1)
muse.description: the complete muse route registration table recovered from rodata: 603 route records across 67 resources / 332 distinct operations. Each record is 24 bytes {path_template*, flags, 0, handler*, 0, csv_descriptor*}. The csv descriptor 'scope,resource,verb[,subparam]' names the operation; the path template carries {param} bindings. Most ops exist twice: unscoped (v1/players/{playerId}/...) and household-scoped (v1/households/{householdId}/players/{playerId}/...). Positional join attempted on the alarms and settings blocks: verb-name pool order matches op-descriptor record order (alarms: getAlarms/fetchAlarm/createAlarm/updateAlarm/snoozeAlarm/removeAlarm at 0x10f9fd50; settings: getAllSettings/getSettingsGroup/updateAllSettings/updateSettingsGroup at 0x10fa1556), and the trailing u32 column contributes one arity slot per name. The spec-pair stream itself groups by b=0x34/0x38 header entries followed by {0x82,type-index} member refs; group count equals verb count (settings: 4 groups of headers + 82-refs for 4 verbs; alarms: groups separated by ae34/1334 markers). Param-name literals do NOT appear inside the alarms or settings pools beyond verb names and default values (PT0H5M0S), so a positional param join cannot be established for these blocks - pool entries carry verbs, not per-param names.
spec_pairs.consumer: CONSUMER FOUND: the layout/validator switch rooted at 0x10927c84 (epilogue tail 0x10927c70) dispatches on the b-field type index (r4): explicit cases 0x4e/0x62/0x70/0x71/0x72/0x120/0x144/0x146 with a default branch for indices < 0x13a that bitfield-decodes a packed member descriptor (rlwinm/slwi/or chains) into {count, byte-size} pairs stored at consecutive state slots (0x348/0x34c here, parallel slots 0x190/0x194, 0x330/0x334, 0x340/0x344, 0x380/0x384). So each spec entry {a=field_id, b=name_table_index} declares one member; the switch resolves the declared type into the member runtime layout.

Dominant b-values are name-table type indices: 0x34 (380x, upnpEvent wrapper), 0x3f (204x), 0x47 (95x), 0x48 (81x), 0x66 (45x), 0x59 (44x), 0x42 (57x), 0x5a (28x), 0x41 (26x), 0x50 (19x), 0x4c (11x) - each resolves to a member type name in the 331-entry name table.

dispatch_mechanism.flow: dispatcher reads *(this->vt+32) exec slot; if == f_109ec9e0 (null stub returning 0) -> result 90 ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_COMMAND; else bctrl the real exec; result object built via setter family 0x109dbxxx; iterates sub-target objects at stride 304 (IBT fan-out); refcounted via lwarx/stwcx.

dispatch_mechanism.exec_family: f_1015xxxx generated serializers: install primary+secondary vtables (secondary-vtable back-offset pattern), then walk member arrays at obj+92..+96 and obj+144..+148 serializing each member: household/VRC/registration ops exec by serializing their descriptor into the lechmere envelope
dispatch_mechanism.auth_gate: f_109db080 (tag "museauth") is invoked inside dispatch: emits "Secure connection required" (cmd needs WSS/secure transport), "Credential is missing", "Scope is insufficient", "Client auth exception": the enforcement point of the per-op role/scope model; result codes flow back through the 107-entry muse_result_codes table

spec_pair_decode_v2.structure: {u32 a, u32 b} runs terminated by {ffffffff,ffffffff} inside each op-descriptor block, positioned between the 23-slot vtable and the verb literals + count fields
spec_pair_decode_v2.observed_grammar: entries are bimodal: {0x82, 0x21-0x6a} (a=const, b=index-like value across 74 distinct values) vs {X, 0x34} (b=const 0x34, a=wide id space 0x13-0x141 incl. the unique ascending ids previously read as cmd-ids) plus small {n,n} pairs (counts) and occasional b=0x36/0x38/0x33/0x6a/0x4e variants
spec_pair_decode_v2.working_model: INFERRED: serialization schema ({field_id, schema_tag=0x34} declare fields; {0x82, type_index} entries reference param/field types (type-code enum 0x21-0x6a); consumed by the f_1015xxxx serializer-execs which walk the member arrays. a=0xae common-field marker vs unique ids = field identity, not cmd-id) revises the earlier per-OP cmd-id hypothesis; the unique-id correlation with lechmere-numbered ops may still hold if field-ids double as cmd-field keys
spec_pair_decode_v2.unresolved: field-name bindings per entry index (verb/param literal runs are catalogued but not yet joined to entry indices); the tag-enum NAMES are data-model vocabulary - no code dispatch on tag values exists, so names must come from the schema producer (build-time), not the binary's control flow
spec_pair_decode_v2.decoded_block_structure: op-descriptor blocks decode further: N x 0x80-byte op records (e.g. alarms: 6 recs @ 0x10f9f8c4..fc44, each {2 data ptrs, 0x109c9854, vtable_ptr, ~9 thunk ptrs into 101c06xx, shared 109d9770, per-op vtable ptr, thunks, 109d973c x2, 10ac45xx impl-vtable, ffffff88, 0, then 10acXXXX impl ptr, 10acXXXX, 109e8570, 109e857c, 109e858c, 0, 0}) followed by a shared 12-ptr block, then the {u32,u32} spec-pair stream terminated by ffffffff/ffffffff, then zero padding + a u32 op-count (alarms: 2), then the verb-name string pool + default-value literals (snoozeAlarm default 'PT0H5M0S' ISO-8601 duration sits in the pool after the verb names). The 101c06xx entries are trivial this-adjusting vfunc trampolines (stwu/addi/blr), confirming the records are vtable-bound polymorphic op descriptors.
spec_pair_decode_v2.pair_tag_hypothesis: b=0x34(52)=name_table[52]='upnpEvent' dominates the second slot; {0x82,T} pairs have T in 0x21-0x6a which all index the name table -> the pair stream is {tag_or_fieldid, name_table_index}; first slot alternates between unique ids (0x13..0x141 = likely field/verb numeric ids) and const tags (0x82, 0x86, 0xae). Second slot = the declared TYPE name (index into the 331-entry name table). Consistent with 'serialization schema': {field_id, type_tag} where type_tag 0x34 is the common upnpEvent wrapper type.
spec_pair_decode_v2.consumer_layout_dispatch: the spec-stream consumer found: dispatch rooted at 0x10927d24 (fn body ~0x10927c70+) is a per-member LAYOUT/validator switch keyed by name-table index (r4), with r5 carrying a packed member descriptor/value. Default branch (index<0x13a) decodes r5 bitfields (rlwinm/slwi/or chains) into {count,byte-size} pairs stored at consecutive slots of a state object (offsets 0x190/0x194, 0x330/0x334, 0x340/0x344, 0x380/0x384...): i.e. it computes member byte offsets into the runtime object. Special-cased indices: 0x118='track'/0x119='trackQuality' store raw u32s at 0x380/0x384 (trackQuality clamped <=0x4000 else saturates at 0x200000); 0x5b='deviceSoftwareUpdateStatus' + 0x5c='diagnosticInfo' pack into bits 0-1 of the word at 0x3ac (rlwimi); 0x8c='hdmiStatus'/0x8d='versionChanged' take value<=2 through converter f_1093bfc0 -> halfword at 0x3a2; 0x14='upnpEvent'/0x47='channelMapPair' store r5 at 0x394. Return codes: 0x2b=43 propagated as an error/skip code, 0 on handled members.
spec_pair_decode_v2.grammar_decoded: full alarms-block decode proves the pair stream IS {member_name_idx, type_name_idx}: {ok,upnpEvent} {ok,upnpEvent} {alarmList,upnpEvent} {alarm,upnpEvent} then {globalError,T}-runs where T cycles through the allowed member payload types (channelMapPair, chirpRequest, accessoryId, none, wiredSubStatus, bluetoothDevice). So: the SECOND slot is the declared payload type (a name-table index of a TYPE entry), the FIRST slot is the member/field name index. 'globalError' is a polymorphic member whose permitted type-set is enumerated as consecutive rows. 'upnpEvent' is the dominant wrapper type for evented members. ffffffff/ffffffff terminates the stream. The per-member applier f_10927c1c(r3=state, r4=member_idx, r5=value, r7=aux) is one slot in the 7-entry object vtable at 0x10f7f724, invoked via vfunc from the stream driver.
spec_pair_decode_v2.extracted: 51 spec-pair streams extracted to reference/muse_spec_streams.md (every muse resource's member→type map. Grammar confirmed: first slot = member/field name index, second slot = declared payload type index (both into the 0x10f97094 table); ffffffff/ffffffff terminates. Verbs/params follow the stream. 'ok' members always carry upnpEvent; 'globalError' rows enumerate the error/variant payload types; named members (alarmList, entitlementsList, zoneDefinition...) carry their typed payload. The 0x10ffca08 stream is a DIFFERENT table (none/accessoryId pairs) likely an enum/identity map, not the member:type grammar).

resolved_findings: Established: {a,b} bimodal grammar, block structure (0x80-byte op records, 23-slot vtable spine, FFFFFFFF terminator), the accessor + serializer-exec consumers, and that tag dispatch is data-driven (no code compares on tag values). Still unknown: field-name bindings per entry index and the boundary between decoded spec pairs and the opaque descriptor tail. Next step: join entry indices to the verb/param literal run order to name each declared field.

Arity-table column census (13 blocks): the u32 run between the ffffffff terminator and the verb-name pool carries one arity word per pool name, repeated per op. Single-word ops: getRelativeTime block (1 verb -> {4}), startSignalling/stopSignalling ({4,4}), triggerSwap/requestSwap ({4,4}), subscribeUser/unsubscribeUser/getEntitlements ({6,6,6}), the clip block (4 names -> {4,4,4,4}). The settings block is the only multi-word form: 4 verbs -> {4,1,6} repeated once per verb, so all four settings ops share an identical 3-slot signature shape. The values do not count spec-pair stream entries (settings: 22 entries vs arity sum 44; subscribeUser: 7 entries vs arity 18), so the column is a declared-signature arity - most consistent with {in_params, out_params, total_fields} style member counts of the op request/response records, single-word blocks degenerating to a total. Whether the 3-word form is {in,out,total} or another triple remains data-model vocabulary: no .text consumer reads the column (same boundary as the spec-pair tags themselves).
spec_pair_decode_v2.tail_decode: OPAQUE TAIL DECODED on the alarms block (0x10f9fc74): after the ffffffff/ffffffff terminator comes a zero pad, a u32 count field (alarms: 2 - its semantic is ambiguous, channel/variant count vs subfield count), then the verb-name string pool as consecutive NUL strings ('getAlarms','fetchAlarm','createAlarm','updateAlarm','snoozeAlarm','removeAlarm') followed by param default literals ('PT0H5M0S' for snoozeAlarm), then the next descriptor block's pointer records (0x10f9fdac). The tail is the verb+default literal pool, not opaque data.
spec_pair_decode_v2.per_op_grouping: the 22 spec entries in the alarms block group per-op: marker entries {0xae,0x34}/{0x13,0x34}/{0x16,0x34} alternate with member runs {0x82,type_index}, yielding ~5 member-groups for 6 verbs (e.g. {0x13,0x34}+{0x82:0x47} vs {0x13,0x34}+{0x82:0x48,0x1,0x0,0x3f} vs {0x86,0x42}+{0x82:0x48,0x3f}). The marker word selects the op variant/dispatch id while the 0x82 run declares that op's typed members - consistent with {field/marker, name_table_type} pairs consumed by the layout switch at 0x10927c84.
spec_pair_decode_v2.tail_grammar: post-terminator tail verified across 7 descriptor blocks: {ffffffff/ffffffff terminator, 0..7 words zero pad, arity-u32 sequence, NUL-terminated name pool, 4-byte pad, next op-descriptor block}. The name pool holds the block's verb and field names verbatim (alarms: getAlarms..removeAlarm + 'PT0H5M0S' default; settings: getAllSettings/getSettingsGroup/updateAllSettings/updateSettingsGroup; registration: getRegistrationStatus/setRegistrationState/transferDevice*; entitlements: subscribeUser/unsubscribeUser/getEntitlements; fields: volumeRampDownSeconds/cancelAudioClip/clipMetadata/audioClips).
spec_pair_decode_v2.arity_table: the u32s between pad and name pool are a small-integer arity table keyed to the spec groups: observed uniform runs {4}x4 (fields), {6}x3 (entitlements), {2}x6, {4}x5, {4}x2 and one mixed run {4,1,6}x6 (settings, 18 words). Per-name arity holds in the uniform blocks (4 counts for 4 names, 3 counts for 3 names); the settings block packs three values per op signature, consistent with {member-count, signature-flag, spec-entry-count} triples but the exact column meanings are not pinned by any single block.

SEMANTIC INDEX i MAPS TO TABLE SLOT 3+i: the first three pointer-table slots at 0x10f97088 are function pointers (f_10809540...), semantic index 0 = 'none'. 331 name entries, 383 object-spec descriptors across 0x10e9ba80 (96) + 0x10f9f87c (287), ~0x80B each, common accessor +0x58, classIds 1-12. Blob grammar = flat {fieldName, typeName} pairs: field slots carry wire keys (ok leads 170 response specs; globalError 561x; upnpResponse/upnpError for bridge ops; accountError/sessionError/playbackError), type slots carry 'upnpEvent' (the universal value wrapper) or concrete types.
